items.title: Arc's folders are kept, whether or not tab groups are on
items.author: Chahine-tech
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited
items.note: Upstream main is an ancestor of Browse. This does not guarantee every historical hunk survives later changes.
items.body:
The first half of #478, as asked there. The second, Arc's pinned pages as rows, follows separately.

`takeAsleep` read the setting as the pages arrived and gave up the folder when tab groups were off:

```swift
guard grouping, let folder else { return nil }
```

So the name never reached the session. Turning tab groups on afterwards found nothing left, and the only way back was to bring Arc over again, which nothing in the app tells you. The session already keeps groups whether or not they are shown, and says so:

> Written whether or not groups are turned on, so turning them off loses nothing.

Now the import does the same. Nothing is shown while the setting is off: every place that draws a group is already behind `prefs.usesTabGroups`, and `arrangeGroupedTabs` has its own guard, so no tab moves.

## Checked

`Tests/arc_folders.py`, in the shape of the others: it writes a made-up Arc into the world's own Import folder, a space whose pinned list is two folders of pages, and asks the import for its spaces with tab groups off.

```
  ok   the pages came in
  ok   their folders are in the session, with groups off
  ok   and every page is in one
  ok   the names are still there once groups are on
4 passed, 0 failed
```

On main, from a worktree, three of those fail with an empty list:

```
  FAIL their folders are in the session, with groups off []
  FAIL and every page is in one 0
  FAIL the names are still there once groups are on []
1 passed, 3 failed
```

`swift build` adds no warnings.

Measured on my own Arc profile before writing any of this, which is what sent me looking: an import with tab groups off gave 11 flat tabs and no Basics or SRE, turning the setting on afterwards changed nothing, and the same import with it on gave both folders and their eleven pages.

items.title: Keys in the ⌃Tab switcher, off unless turned on
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Later, after #480
items.note: Stack includes #480; only its incremental switcher actions are new. Keep optional and avoid double-counting its diff.
items.body:
Split out of #480, as asked in review. **It builds on #480**, so until that merges, this diff also shows #480's commits. Only the last commit is new here.

These keys change the switcher everyone uses, so they sit behind a switch: **Settings › Tabs › Keys in the tab switcher** (`switcher.keys`), off by default. With it off, the switcher behaves exactly as before, and any other key still puts it away.

### With it on

With ⌃ still held, a letter acts on the selected card. Once the pointer has moved, that's the card under it. Each letter does what its ⌘ key does to the tab on screen:

- **⌃W** closes the card. A tab closes as ⌘W closes it, and a split pair closes both pages, since the pair is one card. A pinned tab that isn't on screen is put down and keeps its card. A moon closes its small window. The card leaves the switcher and the selection moves on. Closing the card the gesture started on ends the gesture, just as ⌘W would there.
- **⌃R** reloads the card's page.
- **⌃M** mutes or unmutes it, and the card shows a crossed-out speaker.
- **⌃O** on a moon moves it into the row, like its own Open in Search.

A line under the grid lists the keys, and shows ⌃O only while a moon is selected.

`TabSwitcher.Action` reads the letter; `Browser.act` and `LittleWindow.act` carry it out for whichever switcher the card is in. The switcher can stay up after ⌃W because closing a background tab doesn't change the active tab, and any change of active tab cancels the switcher. For the same reason, a pinned tab that isn't on screen gets `tab.rest()` directly: `close(_:)` on a pin always selects another tab.

### Checked

- `./build.sh` with Xcode beta: builds.
- `Tests/little_switcher.py`, 22 passed. With the switch off, ⌃M closes the switcher and mutes nothing. With it on: ⌃M mutes a tab, ⌃W closes a tab and a moon, and ⌃O moves a moon into the row. The bench's `switcher` verb takes `"keys"` to flip the switch.
- `Tests/tab_switcher.py`, 4 passed.
- Not checked by eye: the Settings line and the legend on a real screen.

items.title: Claude in Chrome sign-in fails, claude.ai page can't message the extension
items.author: cunyiles
items.decision: Historical issue: closed; not independently revalidated
items.note: Closed state alone does not establish resolution; inspect body/discussion if reopening.
items.body:
Hi.

Claude in Chrome (`fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn`, 1.0.94) can't finish sign-in in Search. After I approve on claude.ai, the page shows "Authorization failed. This isn't working right now."

Steps:
1. Install Claude in Chrome in Search 1.0.4 (macOS 27.0.1).
2. Click sign in in the side panel. It opens `https://claude.ai/oauth/authorize?client_id=dae2cad8-...&redirect_uri=chrome-extension://fcoeoabgfenejglbffodgkkbkcdhcgfn/oauth_callback.html&...`
3. Approve. Authorization failed.

The extension has no `oauth_callback.html`. The claude.ai page hands the result to the extension with `chrome.runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, { type: "oauth_redirect", redirect_uri })`, and the extension takes it in `runtime.onMessageExternal` only from `https://claude.ai`. Manifest allows it:

```json
"externally_connectable": { "matches": ["https://claude.ai/*", "https://*.claude.ai/*"] }
```

In Search the claude.ai page has no `chrome` object at all:

```
> typeof chrome?.runtime?.sendMessage
ReferenceError: Can't find variable: chrome
```

The extension side is already there. `search-shim.js` wraps `runtime.onMessageExternal` (line 908). Only the page side is missing.

Expected:
- Pages matching an extension's `externally_connectable.matches` get `chrome.runtime.sendMessage(extensionId, message)` and `chrome.runtime.connect(extensionId)`.
- Messages arrive in `runtime.onMessageExternal` / `onConnectExternal` with `sender.origin` and `sender.url` set.

Thanks

items.title: Each checkout's build tests in a world of its own
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Adapt with missing cleanup
items.note: Align app/bench/fresh per-checkout worlds after fixing Browse paths. Review explicitly requests listing/cleaning orphan test worlds; current patch has not supplied it.
items.body:
Follows #476, which gave the test harness's worlds a per-checkout tag. The one shared world left was the test world itself. `SEARCH_PROBE=1`, a run straight from the build folder, `./fresh.sh` and `./bench --test` all used `Search (test)`, whichever checkout the build came from. Two sessions testing at once, each from its own worktree, shared its socket, settings and stores, so `./bench --test` could drive the other session's build. I found one doing exactly that while checking #492.

## What changes

- **`Store.world`:** the test world is now the checkout's own, `test-<tag>`, where the tag is the first eight hex digits of a SHA-1 of the checkout's real path. That's the same tag `Tests/split_view.py` uses. The app finds its checkout from its own executable: the folder holding the nearest `build/` or `.build/` (so `build/intel/` works too). It resolves the path with `realpath`, as Python's `resolve()` and bash's `pwd -P` do. `URL.resolvingSymlinksInPath` drops `/private`, which would give a different tag for a checkout under `/tmp`.
- **Builds outside any checkout** (an installed app run with `SEARCH_PROBE=1`) keep the plain `test` world, as before.
- **`./bench --test`** and **`--world test`** go to this checkout's test world.
- **`./fresh.sh`** wipes and opens this checkout's test world. It passes the full name as `SEARCH_PROBE`, so the app lands in the same world. The plain world's special case (no hash) went with it, since `fresh.sh` always runs a checkout's build.
- **The bench skill's docs** say where the test world now lives.

Named worlds (`SEARCH_PROBE=NAME`, `--world NAME`, the unit tests' worlds) are unchanged.

## Worth knowing before merging

The test world moves, so anything kept in the old `Search (test)` stays there: sign-ins made for testing, installed extensions, and saved test passwords (the keychain label follows the world name, see `Vault.swift`). Each checkout starts its test world empty. `./fresh.sh` and a sign-in bring it back per checkout. If that's a problem for how you test, copying `Search (test)` into a checkout's world once would carry it over. I haven't added that, since it would bring back the sharing this removes.

## Checked

- **The three names agree:** for this worktree, `bench`'s `test_world()`, `fresh.sh`'s line, and the app launched with a bare `SEARCH_PROBE=1` all give `test-4eb239dd`. `./bench --test tabs` reached that app.
- **The stores agree:** the WebKit store the app made is the one `fresh.sh` computes and wipes.
- **The shared world wasn't touched:** another session was using the plain `Search (test)` world during the run, and its folder was left alone.
- **Named worlds still work:** `fresh_window.py` passes 7/7. No new build warnings.

items.title: The folded column's shadow falls from its ground, as the strip's does
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited
items.note: Upstream main is an ancestor of Browse. This does not guarantee every historical hunk survives later changes.
items.body:
In full screen, the folded column lagged as it slid out over the page. One cost is its shadow. The column cast the shadow from its own rows, so on every frame of the slide the shadow was drawn again from every row, icon and title, down the column's whole height. In full screen that height is the whole screen's.

## What changes

**The column's shadow falls from its ground.** #462 gave `FoldShadow` a `behind` mode that casts the shadow from `Palette.ground` laid under the view, and the strip across the top already used it. The column now does too. Its own ground is opaque, so the shadow is the same rectangle, and it still fades with the slide.

**The ground slides away with the column and the strip.** With `behind`, the ground stayed where the column or the strip had been as it slid away: a blank band over the page for nearly a second. That was already the case for the strip on `main` (#462), and the first commit here spread it to the column. The transition was `.move(...).combined(with: .casting(...))`. That put the ground outside the move's offset, which moves only what it wraps. Combining them the other way round, `.casting(...).combined(with: .move(...))`, carries the ground along.

## Testing

- Builds on `main`.
- `./bench film unpeek` with the ground temporarily painted red:
  - Before: the red ground stood still while the tabs and the column slid off, for about 0.9 s.
  - After: it slides up with the strip, and none shows under the column at any point.
- `./bench fold` draws the column at rest over red, with the column on the left and on the right. It's solid, and the shadow falls from its inner edge, as before.
- Measured by hand, in real full screen on a 120 Hz MacBook Pro: the edge slide missed 2 to 11 vsyncs per slide. The same slides in a normal window of the same size missed 0 to 2.
- ⌘S folding a column that's on screen has no shadow and is unchanged here. It lags in full screen too (13 to 16 missed vsyncs per fold, against 0 to 1 windowed), which I'm looking at separately.

items.title: A favourite whose site is already pinned is the pin you have
items.author: Chahine-tech
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited
items.note: Upstream main is an ancestor of Browse. This does not guarantee every historical hunk survives later changes.
items.body:
Closes #482.

`takeArc` matched a favourite against a pin by its address, letter for letter:

```swift
for favourite in favourites where !defs.contains(where: { $0.home == favourite.url.absoluteString })
```

A pin wanders. Gmail pinned at `mail.google.com` answers at `mail.google.com/mail/u/0/#inbox`, and `pinDefs` writes down where the pin is when it has no home of its own to write. The two strings differ, the guard lets the favourite through, and Arc's Gmail arrives beside the one already there.

It now compares the site: a favourite whose site is already pinned is the pin you have, however far it has gone from the address it was pinned at. `History.identity` wasn't the right tool here, since the two addresses differ by their path, not their spelling.

Only against the pins that were there before the import, though. Two favourites of Arc's own on one site are two favourites and stay two, which is why the guard keeps its address comparison for the ones it is adding as it goes.

## Checked

`Tests/arc_pins.py` brings the same made-up Arc in twice, with a pin sent wandering in between, the way a site does when it answers somewhere else:

```
  ok   every favourite came in, two of them on one site
  ok   the second import adds no pin
  ok   and there are still three
  ok   the one that wandered kept where it had gone
4 passed, 0 failed
```

On main, from a worktree, the middle two fail and the site case still passes, so it guards the fix without guarding something that already worked:

```
  ok   every favourite came in, two of them on one site
  FAIL the second import adds no pin  pins: 1
  FAIL and there are still three  [example.com/, mail.example.com/mail/u/0/#inbox, example.com/second, mail.example.com]
2 passed, 2 failed
```

`swift build` adds no warnings.

A file or an about: page has no site to compare, and those keep the address comparison they had.

items.title: Split View tests hold up on a busy machine
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited
items.note: Upstream main is an ancestor of Browse. This does not guarantee every historical hunk survives later changes.
items.body:
Three checks in `split_view.py` failed on a busy machine (load average 100 to 350), on `main` as well as on branches: "swap: both pictures travel", "even out: the pages move to even halves" and "case_slice5b ran to the end".

## Why the motion checks failed

The moves never happened, so the samples weren't just too early or too late. `PaneStage.capture` gives WebKit 50 ms to picture the pages on screen, and a slower answer makes the change a cut. Logging each snapshot showed the page that had just entered the pair holding its `takeSnapshot` reply for 1 to 11 seconds, with the other page's replies queued behind it. Enter and leave only picture the page that was already on screen, which answers in about 15 ms, so those checks passed. Swap and even-out picture both pages, so they became cuts. Polling for 3 seconds at 30 ms saw nothing, and even a 1 s deadline still missed.

## What changes

- **`PaneStage.capture`**: when the deadline passes on a test run, the pages still waiting get the stand-in a test run already uses when WebKit returns no picture. Pictures that arrive in time are still used. Outside a test run, a late picture still means a cut, as before. The deadline stays at 50 ms, so layout isn't held back.
- **`sample()`**: counts its looks from the first one that shows motion, waiting up to 3 s, because under load a move can start a few hundred milliseconds after it's asked for. "a tab switch is a cut" still takes its looks after that 3 s and still expects nothing moving.
- **`asked(id)`**: waits up to 10 s for a page's question to reach the app, in place of the fixed 1.5 s and 3 s sleeps in `case_slice5b`. This also tightens "page gone elsewhere: its card goes" and "Split View off: the card is answered as dismissed", which used to pass vacuously when the question hadn't arrived yet.

## Testing

items.title: Esc on a question over a panel answers the question
items.author: karadoganyi
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited
items.note: Upstream main is an ancestor of Browse. This does not guarantee every historical hunk survives later changes.
items.body:
Split out of #471, as asked there, for 1.0.5.

With a bookmarks folder's "Remove?" question up over the bookmarks panel, pressing Esc closed the panel and left the question up. The window's own key handling (`take(_:)` in App.swift) took Escape before the sheet saw it, and treated it as "close the panel in front".

## What it does

`take(_:)` now leaves a key typed into a sheet hanging from the window to the sheet (`event.window?.sheetParent != nil`). This covers every question `Ask` puts up.

## Test hooks (test runs only)

- `probe` reports `sheet`: whether a question is up on the window.
- `press` takes `"sheet": true` to send the key to that question.
- `./bench remove-folder TITLE` puts up the real "Remove?" question for a top-level bookmarks folder, the way its row's Remove does.

## Checked

`Tests/dialog_keys.py`, in a hidden probe in its own world (`sv.use("dialog-keys")`):
- A bookmarks file with one folder of two made-up bookmarks is brought in, and the bookmarks panel is opened.
- The folder's Remove puts the question up over the panel.
- Esc sent to the question leaves the panel open, and both bookmarks stay.

Taking the App.swift line out fails "the panel under the question stays". The probe then shows the panel gone and the question still up, which is the bug.

Not checked in a test: that Esc then cancels the question. That needs the question to be the key window, which a hidden probe never has. It's AppKit's own handling of an alert's Cancel.

items.title: A sign-in window a page opens after asking its server first opens
items.author: Aaditya2605
items.decision: Closed without merge flag: inspect before reuse
items.note: No adoption recommendation from closed state alone; may be declined, superseded, partially incorporated or incorporated outside GitHub merge.
items.body:
## What

draw.io's **Authorize** button, for Google Drive, sends a request to draw.io's server and calls `window.open` with the answer. WebKit counts a click as a user gesture only while the click is still being handled. With `javaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically` off (#207), the late `window.open` was refused, and draw.io said "Allow pop-ups to avoid this dialog". The sign-in window never opened.

## The change

This keeps what #207 is for: no window on load or on a timer. It moves the rule from WebKit into Search, so that the rule can wait for a server's answer:

- `javaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically` is on again, so every `window.open` reaches `createWebViewWith`.
- `createWebViewWith` returns `nil` (the page gets `null`, as before) unless the page had a click, a key, or its right-click menu in the last five seconds. That is Chrome's window. It lets one window through for each click or key.
- `PageView` records the time in `mouseDown`, `keyDown` and `didCloseMenu`. The menu counts because "Open Link in New Window" is a window the page opens too, and the menu can stay open for a while.

## Testing

- `swift build`: no new warnings.
- `Tests/popups.py` (new, in `split_view.py`'s test world), run against a build of `main` and of this branch:

| page | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `window.open` 300 ms after load, no click | refused | refused |
| `window.open` 2 s after a click (the draw.io case) | **refused** | opens |
| a second `window.open` for the same click | refused | refused |
| `window.open` 6 s after a click | refused | refused |

`main` 3/4, this branch 4/4.

items.author: Aaditya2605
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited
items.note: Upstream main is an ancestor of Browse. This does not guarantee every historical hunk survives later changes.
items.body:
## What

With many tabs across the top, a tab narrower than `Metrics.tabTitled` shows only its site's mark and has no close cross. `TabPill`'s comment gives the reason: a cross on something that small would be what a click to pick the tab lands on. So a tab that narrow closed only with ⌘W, a middle-click or the menu.

## The change

The reason holds for every tab but the one you're on: it is already picked, so a click on it picks nothing. That tab alone shows a cross in place of its mark while the pointer is on it, as Chrome does.

- The cross is the same `CloseClick` a titled tab uses, laid over the mark only (22×22). The rest of the tab still edits its address.
- Every other compact tab keeps its mark, so a click to go to one never closes it.
- While the current tab is loading, the cross takes the place of its ring the same way.

## Testing

- `swift build`: no new warnings.
- By hand, in my own build: with the tabs down to their marks, the pointer on the current tab shows the cross, and a click on it closes the tab. The other tabs show no cross.

items.title: Download Linked File in the right-click menu saves the file
items.author: Aaditya2605
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited
items.note: Upstream main is an ancestor of Browse. This does not guarantee every historical hunk survives later changes.
items.body:
## What

**Download Linked File**, in a link's right-click menu, did nothing: no save panel, no line at the bottom of the window, no file. The item is WebKit's own; Search doesn't add it.

WebKit does fetch the file (the server sees the request). Then it hands the download to `_webView:contextMenuDidCreateDownload:`, a navigation delegate method outside the public framework (`WKNavigationDelegatePrivate`). It does not come as a navigation action with `shouldPerformDownload`, which is what the comment in `decide()` expected. `Browser` doesn't answer that method, so the download had no delegate, and the file went nowhere.

## The change

- `Browser` answers `_webView:contextMenuDidCreateDownload:` and hands the download to `keep(_:from:)`, as `didBecome download:` does. From there it is an ordinary download: the save panel when Settings asks, the Downloads list, "Saved … Show in Finder", and a private tab's download left out of the list.
- The comment in `decide()` no longer names Download Linked File, and points to the new method. Download Image and the `download` attribute are left as they were; I didn't check those.
- This is the same pattern as `_webView:saveDataToFile:…` for the PDF bar's download button.

## Testing

On macOS 26.6.1:

- A standalone `WKWebView` in an off-screen window, a right-click on a link, and the menu's `WKMenuItemIdentifierDownloadLinkedFile` picked as the menu opens. Run with a delegate that answers the method and with one that doesn't:

| delegate | what arrives |
|---|---|
| without the method | the server gets the request; the delegate gets nothing for it (no navigation action, no download) |
| with the method | `contextMenuDidCreateDownload`, then `decideDestination`, then `downloadDidFinish` with the file's 6 bytes |

- In Search: right-click › Download Linked File on a local test page opens the save panel, saves the file, lists it in Downloads, and "Show in Finder" selects it. Before the change, the same steps did nothing. (Tried in my own build, which has this same method calling that build's `keep(download)`.)
- `swift build`: no new warnings.

items.title: Allow asynchronous POST sign-ins after trusted user interaction
items.author: quanru
items.decision: Adapt and validate
items.note: Preferred delayed-popup fix with per-tab/frame single-use gesture grants and POST preservation. Native long-held context menu and real portal acceptance remain.
items.body:
Closes #511.

Asynchronous POST sign-ins can open one new tab after a real user interaction, preserving WebKit's original popup configuration and POST body. The short-lived grant lives in Search's isolated world and is bound to the receiving tab and native frame origin; synthetic events cannot create it.

### Review changes at `a3c4abe63706afe4be1168cf8f4549d4b2eb83dc`

- Opaque origins have no shared origin key. Their activation can authorize the main frame, never a sibling subframe.
- Repeated keydown and keyboard-generated repeated clicks do not re-arm the grant.
- A click following an input in the same frame within five seconds cannot create a second grant after consumption.
- An allowed main-frame navigation revokes permission before unload handlers run; commit also clears it.
- The shared extension-page controller routes gestures through `message.webView` and its owning browser/tab, rather than whichever tab installed the relay last.
- A real native context menu retains the frame binding and single-use rule beyond five seconds. Closing a menu cannot restore consumed or navigated-away permission.

### Exact revision validation

[Hosted Intel Mac job](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/37876782452/job/113647091011) passed 18 focused Swift tests, a Release build, eight native popup cases and five upstream native link-menu checks.

`python3 Tests/popups.py` uses a disposable hidden probe and local synthetic pages. It passed: load-time open refused; next-page and unload opens refused after navigation; a two-second delayed open allowed once; asynchronous POST preserving `assertion=fake-test-only`; expired activation refused; repeated cross-origin ad-frame requests refused.

`python3 Tests/link_menu.py` passed the existing native menu actions and tab placement checks. **A menu kept open for more than five seconds is still unverified interactively.** `python3 Tests/popups.py --serve` provides the local fixture and manual instructions; the automated run prints this limitation explicitly. The maintained menu probe scheduling was restored rather than changing production behavior to accommodate the test. The run uses no real accounts or model calls.

Earlier installed Beta verification reached the affected SAML destination; that is historical evidence, not a fresh check of every review change. The real-account screenshot remains private. The exact revision job above is authoritative for the current automated coverage.

items.title: Add browser-wide HTTP and SOCKS5 proxy settings
items.author: standby2025
items.decision: Hold: incomplete privacy scope
items.note: Only WebKit stores proxied; URLSession services remain direct. Review requires all traffic paths and data-protection keychain handling. Does not implement chrome.proxy or VPN extensions.
items.body:
Search currently has no browser-owned proxy setting. This adds Settings → Proxy so users can send browsing traffic through a local or remote HTTP CONNECT / SOCKS5 proxy without a proxy extension.

Related to #12: this is a browser-level alternative for the underlying proxy use case. It does **not** implement or promise Chrome `chrome.proxy` extension API compatibility, PAC, or per-URL routing.

- Disabled / System clears Search's override and uses system network settings.
- HTTP and SOCKS5 accept host, port, and optional username/password. HTTP uses Network's HTTP CONNECT API, so the server must support CONNECT tunneling.
- Configuration persists in the existing isolated settings store; the password is kept separately in Keychain (including isolation for development/test worlds). Validation and Keychain failures leave the active configuration intact.
- Applies `Network.ProxyConfiguration` to `WKWebsiteDataStore.proxyConfigurations` for the default store, space stores, and private stores. Stores are weakly tracked so private tab data is not retained by the proxy manager.
- Apply updates existing stores and future stores without restarting or replacing WKWebViews, preserving tabs, navigation history, and sessions. Reload pages to issue requests with the new configuration; existing transfers/connections may finish on the previous route.
- Explicit proxies disable direct failover. This setting covers WebKit browsing data stores; it does not change macOS settings or separate URLSession-based app services.

Validation: `CLANG_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/search-proxy-module-cache swift test --disable-sandbox --filter ProxyTests` built the app and passed all 3 tests. Tests cover validation, persisted settings, existing ordinary/private stores, newly created stores, clearing overrides, and failure atomicity. Existing compiler warnings remain. The restricted environment produced WebKit cache-directory permission warnings; live HTTP/SOCKS5 traffic and Keychain authentication have not been verified end to end.

Suggested manual verification: configure a local HTTP CONNECT or SOCKS5 proxy, load HTTP and HTTPS pages in ordinary/private tabs and a separate space, change/clear the setting with tabs open, and relaunch to check persistence. Test an authenticated proxy and an unreachable proxy as well.

items.title: Allow pop-ups per site: menus that call window.open after a request do nothing
items.author: t-cess
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: #509 is the selected implementation; closed #503 has weaker frame/navigation authorization. Delayed popup support is not proof that every portal or a per-site override is covered.
items.body:
**What I did**
On https://portal.gfmis.go.th/ (the Thai government's financial management portal), after signing in, I clicked a system in the portal's menu.

**What I expected**
The system opens in a new tab, as it does in Chrome, or in Safari once pop-ups are allowed for the site.

**What happened instead**
Nothing. No new tab and no sign that anything was blocked. The menu looks dead.

**Why**
The portal doesn't open the window straight from the click. `goToExternalURL` first sends a request to log the visit (`insetLogApp(...).subscribe(...)`), and only in that callback calls `window.open(url, "_blank")`. By then WebKit no longer counts it as a user gesture, and because `Tab.swift` sets `config.preferences.javaScriptCanOpenWindowsAutomatically = false`, the open is dropped before `createWebViewWith` is ever called. Many enterprise and government portals use this pattern (log first, then open), so they can't be used in Search at all.

**Request**
A per-site way to allow pop-ups, like Safari's Settings › Websites › Pop-up Windows. For example, an "Allow Pop-ups" switch in the site card, next to the new per-site "Don't Float Videos Here" (#433). It would be off by default, so the current blocking stays as it is everywhere else. A small "pop-up blocked" note with an Allow button would also do, if WebKit gives the app a way to hear about the blocked open.

**Environment**
Search 1.0.4, macOS 27.0.

items.title: Media keys go to Search instead of Spotify/Music whenever a tab has a video
items.author: jesusrp98
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: #605 addresses paused media only through script interposition; verify actual Spotify/Music handoff and native Browse PiP before adopting.
items.body:
When a tab has played a video, the play/pause, next and previous keys on my keyboard (and AirPods taps) go to Search instead of the app I'm actually listening to, in my case Spotify.

Steps:
1. Play something in Spotify, then pause it
2. Open any YouTube video in Search, play it for a bit, then pause it
3. Press play/pause on the keyboard

Expected: Spotify starts playing again
Actual: the YouTube video in Search resumes

It stays like that until Spotify plays something again. So a paused tab I forgot about in the background keeps taking my keys. Would be great to have a switch to stop Search from taking the media keys, something like Chrome's "Hardware Media Key Handling" flag.

I dug into it a bit. It looks like WebKit registers the app as macOS's "Now Playing" app from its GPU process whenever an unmuted video or audio element plays, and it keeps that registration after the video is paused. There doesn't seem to be a WebKit setting to turn it off. The only thing that drops it is the element being muted. So one possible fix for the paused case: a page script that mutes paused media elements (they're silent anyway), unmutes them when they play, and hides the change from the page. From what I tested, macOS then hands the keys back to the previous app right away.

While a video is actually playing I couldn't find a way around it without breaking playback. Turning off the GPU process for media does stop it, but then video fails with `NotSupportedError`. So that part might need a change on WebKit's side.

macOS 27, Search at d8c33c8

items.title: Recover stale content-script runtime ports before sending
items.author: quanru
items.decision: Closed without merge flag: inspect before reuse
items.note: No adoption recommendation from closed state alone; may be declined, superseded, partially incorporated or incorporated outside GitHub merge.
items.body:
## Problem

DeepAsk can remain at “正在准备回复…” (preparing reply) indefinitely after sending a question through an existing content-script runtime port. In an installed Search Beta reproduction, that port received no messages while a newly connected UI_PORT received AGENT_STATUS_RESPONSE in 88 ms and the worker still answered a ping. This suggests a lost route for an existing port; the precise WebKit process/idle trigger has not been established.

The current content-script branch returns before the extension-page worker checks. A worker-wide ping also cannot identify a stale port while the worker is responsive on another connection.

## Change

- Before the content-script return, install internal runtime-port health handling in both sending and receiving contexts.
- Before sending on a new port or after five seconds without incoming traffic, queue a snapshot of the unsent messages and probe that same connection.
- If the probe is unanswered for ten seconds, reconnect once and deliver the queued messages only after the replacement acknowledges. If that also fails, emit onDisconnect.
- Never replay messages already passed to WebKit. Explicit caller disconnect cancels pending work without notifying that caller.
- Filter the private probe/ack messages from extension listeners, preserve listener registration/removal, and leave external-extension connections native.
- No periodic keepalive and no additional permissions or dependencies.

## Verification

- On this branch based directly on upstream main: `swift test --filter ExtensionPortHealthTests` — 4 tests passed. Coverage includes idle recovery, ordering and no replay of delivered requests, bounded failure, argument snapshots, explicit disconnect, probe filtering, and external connections.
- On the fork's Beta integration branch: the four new tests plus the existing port-numbering and worker-recovery tests passed (6 total).
- Installed the signed build in `/Applications/Search Beta.app`, using the existing profile and DeepAsk 1.1.46. A UI-submitted diagnostic question received the actual model reply `OK`.
- In that installed Beta, temporarily blackholed one native UI_PORT's probe to simulate the observed stale route. The shim made two probes, dropped one, reconnected, and the next UI-submitted diagnostic question received the actual model reply `RECOVERED`. This is controlled fault injection, not proof of the original WebKit lifecycle trigger.
- Restored the diagnostic hook, disconnected diagnostic ports, closed the diagnostic page and disabled the local bench interface afterward.

Before/after screenshots and metadata were saved locally; they include the user's signed-in browser page, so they are not attached publicly.

## Review readiness — 2026-10-04

This handles individual stale runtime routes; #453 handles confirmed extension worker restart. Neither change is already present in upstream main.

Revision: `2fa2b72da76e20f37ff6f999407c782b833db0cc`. [GitHub-hosted Intel Mac validation](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/37169893100/job/111340503578) passed the scoped Swift regression and Release build.

The Swift run excludes the pre-existing DownloadLifecycleTests harness; [separate download-harness repair validation](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/36993014218) passed. This is not visual Midscene E2E coverage.

The CI Split View model probe fails only on the intermediate-animation-width assertion (91/92). [Unmodified upstream main, Debug build](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/37171014927/job/111343805286) reproduces the same failure, so this failure is also present without these PR changes. The corresponding local Release-model run passed 92/92. CI is still red; failed logs are retained in each job’s artifact, and no visual-animation verification is claimed.

[Combined integration branch](https://github.com/quanru/Search/tree/verify/search-pr-combination-20261004) includes all nine PRs and the import conflict resolution. Its latest version passed 62 scoped Swift tests locally; the preceding version passed all 92 local Split View model checks. These checks do not verify modified mouse drags or live worker recovery.

items.title: A link from another app opens in the small window alone, with no window open
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Closed without merge flag: inspect before reuse
items.note: No adoption recommendation from closed state alone; may be declined, superseded, partially incorporated or incorporated outside GitHub merge.
items.body:
With Settings › General › Open links from other apps in a small window turned on, a link clicked while Search had no window open still brought the browser's window up. If Search wasn't running, the page went into the browser's window, and no small window opened at all.

## Why

The setting was checked in only one place, the `deliver` closure in `Links.hand(to:)`, and too late on both paths:

- **Search not running.** `deliver` doesn't exist until the scene's window has appeared, so the link waited in `waiting` and `summon()` built the browser's window. `hand(to:)` then put the waiting link into that window with `arrive`, which never checks the setting.
- **Search running, no window open.** `deliver` called `Browsers.ensureWindow()` first, which brings a window back, and checked the setting after that. The small window opened, with the browser's window already up behind it.

## What changed

- `Links.take` opens the small window first, before `deliver` or `summon`, so no browser window is brought back or made. A small window needs a browser for its space and tab delegate, but not that browser's window, and `Browsers.acting` falls back to the scene's browser, which exists before any window does. The check in `deliver` is gone.
- `LittleWindow.keep()` (Open in Search, ⌘O) gets its browser from `Browsers.ensureWindow()`. With no window open, a window comes back and takes the page. Before, it moved the page into a browser with nothing on screen.
- `LittleWindow` drops its stored `browser`, which nothing read any more.

At launch, `applicationDidFinishLaunching` builds a window when it finds none. That check still leaves the small window alone because macOS delivers the link first. A throwaway AppKit app that logged the order for `open -a App.app https://…` showed `willFinish → GURL → didFinish`, so the small window already exists when the check runs.

## Testing

- `./build.sh` builds clean, with no new warnings.
- In a named probe world with the setting on: I closed the only window and handed in a link with `bench windows link`. It opened in a small window, and the row stayed as it was. `bench little keep` moved the page into the row, replacing the blank tab. A second link, closed with `bench little close`, left the row alone.
- Not covered by the bench: a link that launches Search. Probe runs ignore links from other apps on purpose, so I checked the launch order separately, as described above. I haven't watched it on screen yet.

items.title: Proposal: Allow inactive tabs to pause without reloading when reopened
items.author: lulkebit
items.decision: Needs coordination
items.note: Preserving live pages trades away memory savings. #448 only changes sleep timing and does not implement suspension/resume without reload.
items.body:
## Problem

When I return to a tab that has gone to sleep, the page reloads and rebuilds its interface. It feels like closing the tab and opening it again, rather than resuming where I left off.

To reproduce:
1. Open a page and interact with it.
2. Switch to another tab and leave the first one inactive until it sleeps.
3. Return to the sleeping tab.

I would expect the existing page to resume, keeping its current state. Instead, the page loads again.

The current implementation saves the interaction state and a snapshot, then discards the WKWebView. Restoring those into a new view cannot preserve the complete running state of a web app.

## Proposal

Offer an option to keep inactive pages in memory while letting WebKit suspend their background work.

- Retain the existing WKWebView when a tab becomes inactive.
- Use WebKit's native inactive scheduling policy to pause background work.
- Reattach the same view when returning to the tab, without starting a new navigation.
- Keep the current unloading behavior available for users who prioritize lower memory usage.

Search already detaches background views, and WebKit's default inactive scheduling policy is suspension, so much of the foundation appears to exist.

Following CONTRIBUTING.md, the new behavior could start as opt-in and disabled by default. Ideally, it would fit into the existing tab sleep setting rather than require another independent switch.

## Trade-off

Keeping pages alive uses more memory than unloading them, but preserves their running state and avoids Search-triggered reloads during normal tab switching.

Reloading may still be necessary if WebKit or macOS terminates a content process.

Would this direction fit the project?

items.title: fix: preserve utf-8 in injected extension scripts
items.author: K-NRS
items.decision: Adopt in staged extension batch
items.note: UTF-8 script fix and stamp-on-success; triggers re-preparation of installed extensions. Add requested failure-retry explanation and test mixed encodings/failed preparation.
items.body:
Backpack 0.10.216 can fail to register its wallet provider on a windows-1252 page: WebKit decodes its injected UTF-8 script using the host page’s encoding, corrupting Unicode regex ranges and throwing `Invalid regular expression: range out of order in character class`. Loading the same script as UTF-8 registers the provider correctly.

During extension preparation, add a UTF-8 signature to valid non-ASCII JavaScript resources. Preserve existing signatures, ASCII, non-UTF-8 files, hashbang scripts and files outside the package. Bump the preparation stamp so existing installations receive the correction, and only record the new stamp after preparation succeeds. The host page’s encoding and its own scripts remain unchanged.

Validation:
- Added a real WebKit/unpacked-extension regression: it failed on the legacy page before the fix; all 8 checks pass after it, including a UTF-8 page, the site’s own legacy script, byte-preservation cases and repreparation after a stale stamp.
- `swift build -j 2` passes. Final clean-commit `swift test --skip-build`: 47 tests, 0 failures. An earlier full run hit a download-lifecycle timing timeout; both its isolated retry and the final complete run passed.
- With the real Backpack package in an isolated profile, the legacy page now exposes its Solana and Ethereum providers. Its startup request receives `needs-onboarding`. No wallet import, signing or complete dApp connection approval was tested.

The separate worker-to-popup notification failure observed on the older installed build is already addressed upstream by 1e8eb0c and its follow-ups; this PR does not duplicate that change. Adding a signature changes resource bytes, so packages validating precomputed script-integrity hashes are a compatibility consideration; integrity checks are not bypassed.

items.title: A file under /private/tmp or /private/etc opens instead of staying blank
items.author: arvakme
items.decision: Closed without merge flag: inspect before reuse
items.note: No adoption recommendation from closed state alone; may be declined, superseded, partially incorporated or incorporated outside GitHub merge.
items.body:
## What

A local page or PDF opened by an address like `file:///private/tmp/page.html` stayed blank: the tab showed loading forever, with no error. The same file opened as `file:///tmp/page.html` loads. It affects anything under `/private/tmp` and `/private/etc`, where the address has `/private` in it.

`open(_:)` picks the folder the page may read from with `standardizedFileURL`, which turns `/private/tmp` into `/tmp` and `/private/etc` into `/etc`. The file is still spelled `/private/tmp/...`, and WebKit compares the two as written. It finds the file outside its folder and loads nothing, without a failure callback. This came in with the read-folder rule from #366.

## The change

- The choice of folder moves into `URL.readableFolder`. The standardized path is still what decides whether a folder is too wide (home, `/`, `/Users`, a volume); what is handed to WebKit is the folder spelled as the file is.
- `LocalFileTests` covers the spelling and the two rules that were already there (a file in a wide folder reads only itself; a file beside its pictures reads its folder). Before the change the `/private/tmp` and `/private/etc` cases fail.
- A line under Unreleased › Fixed.

## Testing

On macOS 26.6.1, in a test world driven with `./bench`:

| address | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `file:///private/tmp/…/page.html` | blank, loading forever | loads, title and text there |
| `file:///private/tmp/…/doc.pdf` | blank, loading forever | `application/pdf` |
| `file:///tmp/…/doc.pdf` | loads | loads |

`swift test`: 50 tests, no failures. `swift build` with no new warnings.

items.body:
**What I did:** typed a path to a file on this Mac in the address field: `/Users/me/Documents/report.pdf`, or `~/Documents/report.pdf`, then Return.

**What I did:** opened a local text file from the address field, by its address: `file:///…/hosts` (a copy of `/etc/hosts`), a `Makefile`, `.zshrc`, `Dockerfile`, or a file ending in `.swift`, `.yml`, `.toml`, `.log`, `.sh` or `.ts`.

items.title: A path typed in the address field opens the file instead of being searched
items.author: arvakme
items.decision: Closed without merge flag: inspect before reuse

items.body:
Fixes #523.

## What

Typing `/Users/me/report.pdf` or `~/report.pdf` in the address field searched the web for it: `Address.url(from:)` found no address in it, and `Browser.destination(for:)` fell through to the search engine. The file didn't open and the path went to the search engine.

## The change

- `Address.url(from:)` answers a typed path with a `file://` address when it starts with `/` or `~/` and names a file that is there. It asks before the check for spaces, since a file's name may have them.
- Only a file that exists counts. `/r/swift` and a path to nothing are searched as before, and a folder is left to the search too: a tab has no page to show for it.
- `Address.swift` stays Foundation-only, as `Tests/HistoryRegression/run.sh` compiles it on its own.
- `TypedPathTests` covers a path with spaces, a `~/` path, a missing path, a folder, `/r/swift`, and that ordinary addresses are unchanged. The two that open a file fail without the change.
- A line under Unreleased › Fixed.

## Testing

On macOS 27.0, in a test world driven with `./bench`:

| typed | result |
|---|---|
| `/tmp/…/my report.pdf` | `file:///tmp/…/my%20report.pdf`, `application/pdf` |
| `~/….pdf` | the file in the home folder, `application/pdf` |
| a path to nothing | no address, as before (searched from the address field) |

`bench` goes through `Address.url(from:)` directly; the address field's Return goes through `destination(for:)`, which asks `Address` first, and I read that path rather than typing into the field.

`swift test`: 51 tests, no failures. `Tests/HistoryRegression/run.sh` passes, and `swift build` adds no warnings.

items.title: Sharing your screen from a web call freezes the whole screen (system SCContentSharingPicker)
items.author: sxivansx
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: #530 adds an app permission gate; its review still requires prompt arbitration and cancellation fixes. It does not fix the macOS picker freeze itself.
items.body:
**What I did:** Joined a web call (e.g. Google Meet / Slack in a tab) and pressed **Share screen**, choosing a whole screen in the macOS picker.

**What I expected:** The picker closes and the screen starts sharing, as in Safari.

**What happened:** The macOS share picker / overlay comes up and the **entire screen locks up**. The pointer still moves but nothing is clickable for a while; it recovers on its own after ~1–10 min, or needs a force restart.

**macOS:** 26.5 (25F71) · **Search:** 1.0.4

---

### What's going on

For a normal website tab, Search's `WKUIDelegate` is `Browser`, which does **not** implement `_webView:requestDisplayCapturePermissionForOrigin:initiatedByFrame:withSystemAudio:decisionHandler:`. (That selector is only implemented on `ExtensionPageDelegate` / the popup / offscreen delegates, for the extension-recording broker in `ExtensionCapture.swift`.)

So for a site, WebKit takes its default path (`UIDelegate::UIClient::decidePolicyForUserMediaPermissionRequest`): with no display-capture delegate it calls `request.promptForGetDisplayMedia(UserChoose)`, which on macOS goes GPU-process → `ScreenCaptureKitSharingSessionManager::promptWithSCContentSharingPicker` → the **system `SCContentSharingPicker`** (driven by `replayd` + `ControlCenter`). I confirmed this path in a local build: `getDisplayMedia` in a Search tab routes straight to the OS picker, no Search UI in between.

The freeze is in that **system** picker/overlay, not in Search's own code. The same `SCContentSharingPicker` overlay is what locks up the screen in Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Discord, Teams and WhatsApp on recent macOS — it's widely reported since Sequoia and into Tahoe 26, and there's a 60 s watchdog inside WebKit (`userPromptWatchdogInterval`) that eventually cancels a stuck prompt, which matches the "unfreezes after a while" behaviour.

References:
- Apple Community — "Screen Sharing overlay causes freezing" (Chrome/Firefox/Safari/Discord/Telegram): https://discussions.apple.com/thread/255863690
- Apple Community — cursor stuck during Meet screen/app share (Chrome): https://discussions.apple.com/thread/256222070
- Electron, same `SCContentSharingPicker` hanging/crashing: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/45306

### So: mostly an OS bug, but a couple of Search-side options

1. **Ask first, like the camera/mic/location card.** Implement the display-capture delegate on `Browser` and show Search's own quiet "Allow *site* to share your screen?" card (reusing `CaptureAsk`) before handing off to the system picker. It doesn't fix the OS overlay, but it keeps an accidental click on a page from dropping straight into the freeze, and it's consistent with how every other permission is handled.
2. **Make sure the pending prompt is cancelled on navigation / tab close** so a wedged picker doesn't outlive the page.

Happy to send a PR for (1)+(2) if that direction fits — it's the same shape as the existing camera/microphone card, just wired to the display-capture selector.

items.title: A local text file opens as text, not as a copy in Downloads
items.author: arvakme
items.decision: Closed without merge flag: inspect before reuse
items.note: No adoption recommendation from closed state alone; may be declined, superseded, partially incorporated or incorporated outside GitHub merge.
items.body:
Fixes #525.

## What

Opening a local text file by its address left a blank tab and put a copy of the file in the Downloads folder, for a `Makefile`, a dotfile like `.zshrc`, a `Dockerfile`, or a `.swift`, `.yml`, `.toml`, `.log`, `.sh` or `.ts`. WebKit gives these `application/octet-stream`, or a type it doesn't show (`application/x-yaml`), and `decidePolicyFor response` answers `.download` for anything `canShowMIMEType` refuses. `README`, `LICENSE`, `.md`, `.py`, `.csv` and `.xml` were already shown.

## The change

- New `LocalText.contents(of:)`: a regular file under 20 MB that reads as UTF-8 text (no NUL byte, nothing that isn't a letter) gives its bytes; anything else gives nil.
- In `decidePolicyFor response`, a main-frame file the window can't show but that reads as text is cancelled and loaded from its bytes as `text/plain`, with the file's own address as `baseURL`. The tab keeps the file's address, and a reload or a wake opens the file again by the same path. Anything else goes the way it did: binaries, other encodings and big files are downloaded, and nothing changes for an address on the web, where a server that says `octet-stream` means a file.
- `LocalTextTests`: text with tabs and non-ASCII, an empty file, binary, Latin-1, the size limit, and a missing file or a folder. The four that show text fail without the class, checked with a stub that answers nil.
- A line under Unreleased › Fixed.

## Testing

On macOS 27.0, in a test world driven with `./bench`, each opened as `file:///tmp/…`:

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `hosts`, `Makefile`, `.zshrc`, `b.swift`, `d.yml`, `g.log` | blank tab, copy in Downloads | `text/plain`, its text, address kept |
| `README` | text | text |
| binary (`urandom`) | downloaded | downloaded |

A reload of the `Makefile` tab still shows it. Not checked: a tab waking from sleep (a bench tab never sleeps), which goes through the same `open` path.

`swift test`: 52 tests, no failures. `swift build` with no new warnings.

items.title: Ask before a website shares your screen (gates the system picker in #528)
items.author: sxivansx
items.decision: Rework before adopting
items.note: Current diff lacks requested shared prompt-busy guard, pending screen cancellation and safe test answer handling. Consent mitigation, not OS picker freeze fix.
items.body:
Relates to #528.

### Why

Today, when a website calls `getDisplayMedia` (Google Meet, Around, any WebRTC call), `Browser` doesn't implement WebKit's display-capture permission method, so WebKit takes its default path and drops the page **straight into the macOS `SCContentSharingPicker`**, with nothing of Search's in front of it. That system picker is also where the whole-screen freeze reported in #528 happens — it's a macOS-level issue that hits Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Teams and others too. Search can't fix the OS picker, but it can stop a page from reaching it on a stray click, and make screen sharing a deliberate yes like every other permission.

### What

A site's screen-share request now goes through Search's own card first, the same bottom card the camera, microphone and location use:

> **127.0.0.1 wants to share your screen**  · Share a Screen · Share a Window · Don't allow

- **Don't allow** → the page gets `NotAllowedError` and the Mac's picker never opens.
- **Share a Screen / Share a Window** → WebKit then shows the Mac's own picker, in single-display or single-window mode, to choose which one (matching Safari's native "Allow to Share Screen / Window" alert).

Details:
- Two allow buttons because the private delegate's decision is Screen / Window / Deny — there's no "let the system offer both," so Search asks which, as Safari does.
- The card is asked over the page's own tab (a background tab waits until you go to it), takes no click in its first half second, and refuses a second page while one is up — same rules as the camera card.
- **Nothing is remembered.** Sharing your screen is said yes to each time, as in Safari.
- **Extension recording is unaffected:** an extension recording through its broker (`ExtensionCapture`) is already approved, so `askedToShareScreen` returns its in-flight decision straight away with no second card.
- No Settings switch — asking before screen share is expected-browser behaviour, like the camera prompt.

### How I checked

`swift build` is clean (no new warnings). `swift test` needs full Xcode for XCTest and I only have the Command Line Tools here, so I verified in a driven probe instead (`./fresh.sh` world, `./bench`):

- A site's `getDisplayMedia` now raises Search's card (`asking = "127.0.0.1 screen"`) instead of going to the Mac picker.
- **Don't allow** (`bench answer noscreen`) → card clears, page gets `NotAllowedError`, the Mac picker never opens.
- **Share a Screen** (`bench answer screen`) → `ScreenCaptureKitSharingSessionManager::promptForGetDisplayMedia - Screen`; **Share a Window** → the picker in Window mode.
- Camera, microphone and location cards still behave as before.

New bench affordance for this: `./bench answer screen|window|noscreen`.

items.title: Too many pinned extensions push the whole sidebar left and cut it off
items.author: Vedaant-Rajoo
items.decision: Historical issue: closed; not independently revalidated
items.note: Closed state alone does not establish resolution; inspect body/discussion if reopening.
items.body:
### What I did

1. Tabs in the column (sidebar), Spaces on.
2. Pinned a few extensions to the toolbar (4, then 6).
3. Dragged the column's edge in to its narrowest width.

### What I expected

The column keeps its layout, and whatever doesn't fit in the row at the bottom is dropped, the way Chrome moves pinned extensions that don't fit into the puzzle menu.

### What happened instead

The whole column slides left and gets cut off on both sides:

- the favicons and the first letters of every tab title are cut off at the left edge
- the first favourite square is gone
- the back button slides under the traffic lights
- at the right end of the bottom row, the puzzle button and the bookmarks button are cut off or gone, so the extension list and the bookmarks can't be opened until you widen the column or unpin something

With 4 pinned extensions everything moves about 19pt; with 6, about 47pt.

Screenshots: wide column, everything fits / narrowest column with 6 pinned / narrowest column with 4 pinned.

<!-- drag the three screenshots here -->

### Why

The row at the bottom of the column (`SideBar.foot` in `Side.swift`) is an `HStack` of fixed 26pt buttons with 2pt between them and 10pt of margin on each side, and `ExtensionButtons` puts every pinned extension in it with no limit. With Spaces on, that row is `28 × pinned + 102` points wide: the space's button, the pinned extensions, the puzzle button and the bookmarks button (plus 28pt while a download is running).

When that's wider than `prefs.sideWidth`, the column's `ZStack` takes the row's width. `.frame(width: prefs.sideWidth)` centres the wider stack in the column, `.clipped()` cuts both ends, and the column's leading-aligned content ends up half the overflow to the left. The numbers line up with the screenshots: at 176pt (`Metrics.sideMin`), 4 pinned is 38pt too wide (19pt shift) and 6 pinned is 94pt too wide (47pt shift).

How many pinned extensions fit before it breaks:

| Column width | Spaces on | Spaces off |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 176pt (narrowest) | 2 | 3 |
| 232pt (default) | 4 | 5 |
| 440pt (widest) | 12 | 13 |

So you don't need to narrow the column at all: 5 pinned extensions at the default width is enough.

### Possible fix

Keep the foot from ever being wider than the column, and let the pinned extensions give way first. Their buttons that don't fit could be hidden and left in the puzzle list, which already lists every extension. The space button, the puzzle button and the bookmarks button stay put. Happy to open a PR if that direction sounds right.

### Environment

- macOS 27.0.1
- Search 1.0.4 (same code on `main` at cddb9cd)

items.title: Closing the last unpinned tab activates a pin instead of leaving a new tab
items.author: kingsleydon
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: Choose #538 for opt-in last-tab behavior. #603 changes the default instead; these are alternatives, not additive fixes.
items.body:
## What I did

1. Keep one or more pinned tabs in the current Space.
2. Open an ordinary (unpinned) tab and make it the active tab.
3. Close all other ordinary tabs, then close this last ordinary tab with ⌘W or its close button.

## What I expected

Stay in the window on an empty/new tab, with the address field ready for the next address or search. The pins should remain available without being selected or woken automatically.

## What happens instead

Search selects a remaining pinned tab instead of leaving an empty/new tab. This makes closing temporary browsing unexpectedly take me into a kept site.

## Code investigation

On current `main` (`cddb9cdd19e64321c95d5e733217799908ad3b52`), `Browser.close(_:)` creates a fresh blank tab only when `tabs.count == 1`. That count includes pinned tabs. With pins still present, closing the last ordinary tab instead removes it and selects its remaining neighbour, which is a pin.

This is related to, but distinct from, #125: that PR fixes bouncing between pins when **closing a pin**, not the last ordinary tab while pins remain.

## Proposed scope

When the active last ordinary tab is closed and only pins remain, leave an empty ordinary tab instead of selecting a pin. Keep existing behaviour when another ordinary tab remains; preserve the pins and Reopen Closed Tab. Closing a background tab should not unexpectedly steal focus from an active pin.

Would treating this as a small tab-lifecycle fix fit the intended behaviour? I can prepare a focused PR with regression coverage.

## Related Zen setting

Zen exposes a related advanced preference in `about:config`:

`zen.workspaces.open-new-tab-if-last-unpinned-tab-is-closed`

Its [official documentation](https://docs.zen-browser.app/guides/about-config-flags#new-tabs) says it opens a new tab when all pinned tabs are unloaded and all tabs are closed, and is **disabled by default**. This is a configurable precedent; it is not enabled by default. A [Zen community request](https://github.com/zen-browser/desktop/discussions/7462) also describes the unwanted automatic selection of previously unopened pins.

If Search intentionally prefers selecting a pin, an opt-in setting could be an alternative; otherwise, a small lifecycle fix would make the empty-tab fallback consistent when pins remain.

## Environment / verification

Read directly from my Mac over Tailscale SSH:

- macOS 27.0 (26A428), arm64
- Search 1.0.4, build 202609272118 (`/Applications/Search.app`)

The source explanation above was verified by reading current `main`; a fresh isolated macOS regression run is still pending.

items.title: Leave a new tab when the last tab that isn't a pin closes (opt-in)
items.author: Adithya-Sakaray
items.decision: Prefer over #603 for this behavior
items.note: Optional last-unpinned-tab blank fallback with focused tests; preserve default and background closing.
items.body:
Fixes #537.

With pins in the row, closing the last tab that isn't a pin selects its neighbour, which is a pin: ⌘W on a page you were done with takes you into a site you keep, and wakes it if it was asleep.

Why: `Browser.close(_:)` leaves a new tab only when `tabs.count == 1`, and that count includes the pins. With pins left, the closed tab goes through the ordinary path and its neighbour is selected.

This adds a switch, **Settings › Tabs › Leave a new tab when the last tab closes**, off by default, as the issue suggested and as CONTRIBUTING asks for a change to how the browser behaves (Zen's `zen.workspaces.open-new-tab-if-last-unpinned-tab-is-closed` is the same idea, also off by default). Turned on, the tab on screen with only pins beside it is treated the same as the only tab: a new tab takes its place in the row, the pins stay where they are and are neither selected nor woken, and the page goes into ⇧⌘T as before. As with the only tab, if that tab is already empty ⌘W closes the window.

Unchanged:
- The switch off: a pin is picked, exactly as today.
- Closing it in the background, with a pin on screen: the pin stays on screen.
- With another ordinary tab left: its neighbour is picked, as before.
- Closing a pin (#125's path) is untouched.

Checked on a macOS 15 runner and by hand on a build of this branch:
- `Tests/close_last_tab.py` (new, the split suite's hidden probe): 9 passed, the switch on and off. Without the change it fails "a new tab is on screen, not a pin".
- `Tests/pin_tiers.py`: 32 passed.
- `swift build`: no warnings from this change.
- By hand: with the switch on, pins plus one tab, ⌘W lands on a new tab; ⇧⌘T brings the page back; closing it from the row while on a pin leaves the pin in front. Recording below.

items.title: A window closed while others stay open is freed
items.author: Aaditya2605
items.decision: Adopt early, coordinate windows
items.note: Break ContentView/window retention; clean event monitors/key hooks and Lights entries. Current Browse retains the faulty ownership pattern.
items.body:
## What

A window closed while others stay open was never freed. `Browser.closeAll()` lets its pages go, but the `NSWindow`, its SwiftUI views, its `Browser` and its key monitor all stayed: `NSApp.windows` grew by one for every window opened and closed, and every closed window's monitor still ran on each key press and click.

`ContentView` held its window in `@State`. The window holds its hosting view, and the hosting view holds that state, so the window held itself. Every closure that copied the view (the key monitor, `keyHooks`, the `centreX` that `Lights` keeps) held it too.

## The change

- `ContentView` holds its window weakly, through a small `WeakWindow` box in `@State`.
- `Lights.keep`'s `centreX` is handed the window instead of capturing it.
- `Lights.keep` drops entries whose window is gone. Once windows are freed, a new window can be given a freed one's address, and without this it was taken for the old one and its lights were never put in place.
- Each browser's key monitor is kept in a static table rather than in the view, and `ContentView.forget(_:)`, called from `Browsers.retire`, removes it and the browser's `keyHooks` entry. So the `Browser` goes too.

## Testing

`Tests/closed_windows.py` (on the split suite's harness, hidden, its folder moved to the Trash afterwards) opens and closes a second window 20 times:

| | `NSApp.windows` after each close |
|---|---|
| before | 4, 5, 6, … 23 |
| after | flat |

It also checks that every new window's lights are where the first window's are, and that ⌘L in the window behind opens that window's own field (the monitors that remain still answer for their own window). It fails on main and passes on this branch, on macOS 26.6.1.

items.title: Prevent cross-site tracking, turned off, lets a framed site keep its cookies
items.author: Aaditya2605
items.decision: Fix before adopting
items.note: Current patch sets cookie policy to always and never restores it. Require symmetric on/off policy at runtime and launch, across Spaces; retain private exclusions.
items.body:
## What

With **Settings › Privacy › Prevent cross-site tracking** turned off, a site shown inside another site's page still got no cookies. A Kaltura video in a Brightspace course said "your browser is blocking 3rd party session cookies", with the switch on or off.

The comment on `Store.keepsSignIns` (and the note on #363) says that, turned off, "a site framed in another gets its cookies again". The switch turned off only WebKit's tracking prevention (`_setResourceLoadStatisticsEnabled:`). The store's cookie policy stayed at WebKit's default, which takes cookies only from the main page's site. So the framed site's cookies were still dropped.

## The change

- In `Store.followSignIns`, when the switch is off, the store's cookie policy is set to `.always` too, through `_setCookieAcceptPolicy:completionHandler:` on its `httpCookieStore`. This is the same private-selector pattern as the line above it, with the same `responds(to:)` guard.
- When the switch is on, the policy is not touched. WebKit keeps the policy in the store, so after the switch goes off and on again, the policy stays `.always`. That does not open anything: tracking prevention blocks the framed site's cookies again whatever the policy says. The last check in the test covers this.
- Private tabs are not changed: their store never goes through `followSignIns`.
- One line in CHANGELOG.md, under Fixed.

## Testing

On macOS 26.6.1:

- `swift build`: no new warnings.
- `Tests/cross_site_cookies.py` (new, in `split_view.py`'s test world). A page on `127.0.0.1` frames a page on `localhost`, which sets a cookie, then reports what its server was sent and what its script can read:

| check | this branch |
|---|---|
| prevention on: the frame gets no cookie | passes |
| prevention off: the frame's server gets its cookie | passes |
| prevention off: the frame's script reads its cookie | passes |
| prevention on again, same store: the frame gets no cookie | passes |

On `main`, the two "prevention off" checks fail: the frame is sent no cookie and reads none.

The test needs a new test world to fail on `main`. A world used before keeps the cookie policy from an earlier run in its store, so the bug does not show there.

items.title: Open Link in New Tab leaves you where you are
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited
items.note: Upstream main is an ancestor of Browse. This does not guarantee every historical hunk survives later changes.
items.body:
A link's right-click menu took you to the new tab, so opening one in the background needed ⌘ held or a mouse's middle button. On a trackpad there was no way to do it with a click alone. Safari, Chrome and Firefox all open the menu's new tab in the background.

## What changed

- **Open Link in New Tab** opens the tab behind the one you're on, next to it in the row (`placeForNew`, where a ⌘-click's goes), and joins the source tab's group when tab groups are on.
- Holding **⌥** with the menu open swaps it for **Open Link in New Tab and Go to It**. That's a copy of WebKit's own item, left untouched, so it does exactly what the menu did before.

WebKit finds the link and asks for the tab later, from the page's process, so the menu item can't open it directly. `PageView.openLinkBehind` marks the view for 1 second and hands on to WebKit's action. `createWebViewWith` takes the mark with `takeBehind()`, which clears it on first use. WebKit still finds the link itself, so links in frames, linked pictures and SVG links behave as before.

## Testing

- New `Tests/link_menu.py` (hidden, in split_view.py's test world), through a new bench `linkmenu` command. It right-clicks a link through the page's view and picks the item as the menu comes up, so WebKit makes the tab as it does for a hand. It checks that the default item leaves the current tab in front and puts the new one right after it, and that the ⌥ item goes to the new tab. 5/5.
- `Tests/tab_switcher.py` still 4/4.
- Builds clean, with no new warnings.

items.title: Long addresses scroll with the caret in the tab and the new-tab field (#517)
items.author: razbyskov
items.decision: Already upstream-merged; main inherited

items.body:
Fixes #517.

## Cause
`TabAddressField` and `AddressField` never set `isScrollable` on their cell, so the field editor stayed as wide as the field. Text past the edge was cut off, and the caret, Home/End, ⌘←/→ and clicking couldn't reach it. #421 gave the tab field the width it's offered, which was necessary but not sufficient.

items.title: Document WebKit screen-audio limitations with a capture probe
items.author: BryanZaneee
items.decision: Closed without merge flag: inspect before reuse
items.note: No adoption recommendation from closed state alone; may be declined, superseded, partially incorporated or incorporated outside GitHub merge.
items.body:
Requesting screen sharing with audio does not yield an audio track in the tested WebKit environment. No small production fix has been established.

Adds a standalone synthetic-device probe and documentation covering reproduction, relevant WebKit source, limitations, and next steps. No production behavior or dependencies change. This is an investigation for #540, not a fix; the issue should remain open.

**Validation** — macOS 27.0.1:

- Display capture with `audio: false` and `audio: true` both returned one video track and zero audio tracks.
- The microphone control returned one audio track; the probe completed successfully.
- The probe uses synthetic devices and an ephemeral data store, capturing no real screen or sound. Missing hooks, failed controls, errors, and timeouts fail the run.

Real screen/window consent, system audio, WebRTC delivery, and other macOS versions remain unverified. Any native audio bridge needs a separate design and validation effort.

Related to #540.
