items.body:
When the sidebar is hidden, navigation should remain within reach. This adds optional floating Back/Forward controls and an address field at the top centre of the window, alongside a persistent interface-language selector with French and English support.

### Changes

- Add **Settings → General → Show floating navigation**, off by default and independent of the sidebar. Two compact glass capsules provide Back, Forward, address/search, suggestions and Reload/Stop. They remain centred when the sidebar appears.
- Use native Liquid Glass on macOS 26, with a material fallback on older supported versions and support for reduced motion and transparency.
- Add **Settings → General → Interface language**: System, French or English. Selection is remembered and updates menus and settings immediately. Bundle the French catalogue with the app and preserve interpolation arguments.
- Keep Find on Page clear of the floating controls, adapt settings to small windows, and preserve address focus after toggling navigation.
- Include an optional `build-local.sh` and `LOCAL.md` for a separate local Search build with isolated preferences, browsing data and keychain labels. Official builds keep their existing update behavior.
- Add regression tests and Unreleased changelog entries.

### Validation

- `swift test`: 53 tests passed.
- `./build-local.sh debug`: app built successfully; bundle signature verification passed.
- Checked light/dark appearance, 640-point windows, sidebar visibility, navigation on/off, address editing and suggestions, Back/Forward, Find on Page, and live French/English switching in the running app.

Older macOS fallback rendering, VoiceOver, and reduced-transparency behavior have not been exercised on-device. Historical release notes, extension-provided text, and system dialogs may retain their original language; web page content is unchanged.

items.title: The floating video goes out and comes back in one step
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Do not merge video path
items.note: Optimizes the replaced custom floating-webview pipeline; incompatible direction with Browse native PiP.
items.body:
The floating video now goes out to its little window and back into its tab in one step, whether it's lifted with ⇧⌘P, by switching tabs, or by switching apps.

## Why

Each move showed the page in between states, because the web view changed hosts before the page had been laid out at its new size.

- **Going out:** the little window showed the video at a fraction of its size, then it grew to fill the window. The fraction matched the share of the tab the video had filled.
- **Coming back:** the tab showed the video alone at the little window's size, then the page filled in around it, then the video grew into place about half a second later.

Three causes stacked up:

1. **The page lags its view.** WebKit lays the page out at the new size a few frames after the web view is resized and moved.
2. **The video's picture lags its box.** WebKit draws the picture in another process. When the video's box changes size, it stretches the old picture into the new box for about 300 ms, until that process redraws.
3. **YouTube re-measures late.** YouTube sizes its player at 730×411 first and corrects to 808×454 about half a second later. A plain window resize on a YouTube tab does the same, with no floating involved.

Switching tabs had a fourth: `select` swapped the stage to the new tab before the lift, so the leaving page sat outside every window for about 0.1 s. WebKit threw away everything it had drawn and rebuilt it in the little window. A muted video in that gap didn't float at all.

## What changed

- **The video keeps its tab size while floating.** It's fixed at the window's corner and fitted with `translate(...) scale(min(100vw / W, 100vh / H))` in pure CSS, so WebKit never redraws the picture at another size, going out or coming back. A WebKit without length division in `calc()` falls back to the old `100vw`/`100vh` rule.
- **A cover until the page settles.** The little window opens on a still of the video, cut from a snapshot taken before the lift. The tab lands under a picture of the page as it was left (`tab.cover`). Each cover comes off once the page underneath matches its home size and WebKit has presented that frame, capped at 0.8 s going out and 1.5 s coming back.
- **Leaving a tab no longer drops its page.** The stage keeps the leaving page drawn, at alpha 0, until the little window takes it (`StageView.keep`/`letGo`).
- **Snapshots are capped at about 1.2 MP.** A full Retina snapshot cost 480 ms of CPU painting; capped, it takes about 0.1 s.
- **The bench can film all three ways.** `film float|land … [key|switch|app]` lifts via ⇧⌘P, a tab switch, or leaving the app, and reports when the covers go up and come down, what WebKit has handed over to draw, and whether the page ever leaves a window.

Two private names are used, each guarded with `responds(to:)` or a class-name lookup, the way the repo already uses others: `_doAfterNextPresentationUpdate:`, to know a frame has reached the screen, and WebKit's video layer classes (`WebAVPlayerLayer`, `CALayerHost`), to check the picture is drawn at the size it's shown. Without them the covers still come off, just without those last checks.

## Testing

- **New `Tests/float_settle.py`:** a local page whose player resizes 0.4 s after each resize, like YouTube's. It checks the round trip three ways (⇧⌘P, switching tabs, switching apps) for the covers, the page staying in a window, and the picture's drawn size. 30 passed, 0 failed, five runs. Against the branch before the CSS scaling, exactly the six picture-size checks fail.
- **`Tests/float_video.py`:** 10 passed, 0 failed. Its check now accepts a contain fit, since the video's box is no longer stretched to the viewport.
- **YouTube films, hidden probe, page 1180×780:** going out, the picture is the window's size from the first frame, and the still shows for 130 to 200 ms. Coming back there's no jump, and the page-as-left shows for about 0.5 s while YouTube re-measures.
- **On screen** by hand on YouTube: out by switching tabs and back by returning to the tab, each in one step. ⇧⌘P and switching apps are covered by the films and tests above.
- **Not covered:** Netflix, which needs an account and DRM. The CSS transform replaces Netflix's own centring translate; the rules that keep its subtitles above the video are unchanged. Resizing the little window by pinch or edge drag follows through `vw`/`vh` but wasn't driven in the probe.

items.title: Reading mode in a dark window: follow the appearance, and a light/dark choice in the article
items.author: dima237
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: #564 -> #565 -> #566 is the reader sequence. Unresolved iframe, preload and appearance tests remain in review.
items.body:
In a dark window, reading mode is a white page with dark text, the only white thing on the screen. The site's own stylesheets also stay under the article, so a rule of theirs like `p{color:#222}` decides the text colour rather than the reader's.

Proposal:

- The reader follows the window (`prefers-color-scheme`), so it is dark when Search is, and changes with Settings › Appearance while an article is open.
- The site's stylesheets go with its layout; Search's own `office-*` sheets stay.
- A small light / dark / as-the-window choice sits in the article's corner, faint until hovered and remembered for the next article. Safari's Reader (its Aa menu), Firefox's Reader View and Edge's Immersive Reader all offer a theme there.
- A headline that repeats the title shows once.

No Settings switch is planned: the control appears only inside reading mode, which you turned on yourself. This is separate from #450, which darkens ordinary pages.

A pull request follows, referring to this issue.

items.title: Reading mode keeps an article's charts and its opening photo
items.author: dima237
items.decision: Adapt reader batch 1
items.note: Charts and opening photos; remove arbitrary iframe-in-figure acceptance as requested. Preserve chart/video host allowlist.
items.body:
## What

On an FT article, reading mode drops every chart and leaves an empty band where each was, and the photo the article opens with doesn't come at all. The charts are Flourish frames, and reading mode keeps a frame only when it is a video player, so each went and left its figure and caption behind. The FT keeps the opening photo in a topper beside its `<article>`, not in it.

## The change

All in the reader's script (`Reader.swift`):

- A frame from a chart maker stays (inline beside `players`: Flourish and `flo.uri.sh`, Datawrapper and `dwcdn.net`, Infogram, Tableau, `ig.ft.com`, Google Maps), and so does any frame a page put in a `<figure>`. It keeps the height its own script gave it, read before the page is replaced since that script won't run in the reader (420 when there is nothing above 60 to read); `office-chart` takes it off the 16:9 shape video frames get.
- The opening photo comes first: the first `<figure>`/`<picture>` before the article, looking at most four boxes out, whose picture is at least 400 wide, never in `nav`, `aside`, `footer` or `[role=banner]`. Its pictures are resolved with the article's, and it comes without the topper's classes and styles, which the page's stylesheet would otherwise still lay out as a topper (off to one side, cropped).
- A box left with no text and no media goes, rather than stay as an empty band.
- A line under Unreleased › Fixed.

## Test

The script the app runs (taken out of `Reader.swift`), run on a live FT article in Search 1.0.4, against the same article with `main`'s script — [Tourist taxes on the march](https://www.ft.com/content/e6856a1a-77e4-42b5-bcd8-f91973ca9755):

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Charts | none: three empty bands, each a figure and its caption | all three Flourish charts, at 365, 619 and 600 points |
| Opening photo | missing | first, in the column, with its credit |
| Empty boxes | 3 | 0 |

Also on an FT-shaped page offline, in a WKWebView: a frame in a figure with no height of its own came at 420, an ad frame went. `swift build` adds no warnings.

This and two other reading-mode pull requests (#565 for Bloomberg's head and pictures, #566 for light and dark) touch the same script, so whichever lands second will need a small rebase; I'm happy to do it.

items.title: Reading mode keeps an article's head and the pictures in its buttons
items.author: dima237
items.decision: Adapt reader batch 2
items.note: Media buttons and article headers; add requested metadata/none preload to reconstructed videos. Rebase after #564.
items.body:
## What

On a Bloomberg article, reading mode loses every photo, the opening video, the byline and the takeaways, and shows newsletter boxes:

- Each photo sits in a click-to-enlarge `<button>`, and buttons go as clutter with what they hold.
- The byline, the takeaways, the opening video and the line under the headline sit between the `<h1>` and the text, outside the part chosen as the article.

## The change

In the reader's script (`Reader.swift`):

- A button holding a picture or a video is unwrapped; other buttons still go.
- Head parts between the `<h1>` and the article come along, in page order and quieter than the text (`office-above`): those with byline, takeaways or lede in a class name (in part, whatever the case — `BasicByline_byline__VTyoS`) and an `h2`, as long as they are drawn and not in a menu, a rail or a footer.
- What the page itself hides (`display: none`, unless it holds paragraphs) is left out. Every copy of a box a page keeps for each size of screen is copied into the reader, and a site rule that hid one through an ancestor that isn't copied (`.ArticleBody .copy--mobile`) no longer reaches it there.
- A `<video>` its player fed from the page (a `blob:` address) plays from the plain http(s) `<source>` it names, with controls and never by itself, taken out of its video.js box (which the page's stylesheet still sizes for the player: kept, the box's room for the picture and the picture both took a screen's height). Without such a source it shows its poster; without a poster it goes. The player's copy of the poster beside it goes.
- Short newsletter boxes, and a video.js player's controls and read-outs, are left out.
- A caption and its credit, two spans the site's layout kept apart, are spaced.
- A line under Unreleased › Fixed.

## Test

The script the app runs (taken out of `Reader.swift`), run on a live Bloomberg article in Search 1.0.4, against the same article with `main`'s script — [UK police evacuate area near US air base at RAF Fairford](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-27/uk-police-evacuate-area-near-us-air-base-at-raf-fairford-make-arrests):

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Photos | 1 | 3 |
| Opening video | missing | under the headline, from Bloomberg's HLS stream, with controls, at its own size |
| Byline, takeaways | missing | both, above the text |
| Newsletter boxes | 3 | 0 |

Also on a Bloomberg-shaped page offline, in a WKWebView. `swift build` adds no warnings.

This and two other reading-mode pull requests (#564 for the FT's charts and photo, and light/dark — #563) touch the same script, so whichever lands second will need a small rebase; I'm happy to do it.

items.title: Reading mode follows light and dark, or the look chosen in its corner
items.author: dima237
items.decision: Adapt reader batch 3
items.note: Reader appearance and theme control; rebase after #565, remove duplicate extraction logic, test two split articles and live appearance changes.
items.body:
Closes #563

## What

In a dark window, reading mode is a white page with dark text, and the site's stylesheets stay underneath and win over the reader's colours.

## The change

- `Reader.swift`, the script:
  - Colours come from CSS variables, a light set and a dark one, chosen by `prefers-color-scheme` — or by `data-office-look` on `<html>`, which the reader keeps.
  - The site's stylesheets and adopted sheets go; Search's own `office-*` sheets stay (Find on Page puts its highlight sheet back on its next paint).
  - Before they go, what the page hid is marked and left out, and an inline `<svg>` keeps the size it was drawn at — without that, an icon fills the column.
  - A colour written onto an element is set aside, and an `h1` that repeats the title goes.
- `Reader.swift`, Swift: `Reader.look`, kept in `Store.settings` as `reader.look`, and `ReaderLook`, a light / dark / as-the-window capsule in the article's colours, faint until hovered.
- `Stage.swift`: `Page` shows `ReaderLook` while `tab.reader` is true.
- `Tab.swift`: the chosen look goes on with the script; `didCommit` lets go of reading mode — a link followed out of an article left the tab thinking it was still one, so ⇧⌘R reloaded the new page instead of reading it — and an article brought back as it was left, by going back, is taken as one.
- No Settings switch: the control lives only inside reading mode, which was already asked for (see #563).
- A line under Unreleased › Added.

## Test

- The script the app runs, on a live FT and a live Bloomberg article in Search 1.0.4, with the dark look: ground `#1c1c1c`, text `#e0e0e0`, the reader's own sheet the only one left, one `h1`, no giant icons.
- Offline, in a WKWebView: white with `#171717` text in a light window, `#1c1c1c` with `#e0e0e0` in a dark one; the chosen look wins either way. `ReaderLook` rendered in both appearances.
- `swift test`: 47 tests, no failures. `swift build` adds no warnings.
- Not yet tried by hand: Split View with two articles, and switching Settings › Appearance with an article open.

Dark charts (turning a Flourish chart's colours round so it sits dark with the rest) would be a one-line follow-up once #564 is in.

This and two other reading-mode pull requests (#564, #565) touch the same script, so whichever lands second will need a small rebase; I'm happy to do it. The hidden-copies part is in both this and #565.

items.title: Hold or right-click Back and Forward for every page that way
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Adopt as polish
items.note: Native back/forward menus; verify Escape/outside release cannot trigger an extra navigation. Shares toolbar hunks with #571.
items.body:
Holding Back or Forward did nothing, so the only way to reach a page several steps back was the held swipe (off by default, and capped at 8 pages). Safari and Chrome both list the whole history on the buttons.

Now a hold of 0.35s, or a right-click, on either door opens a menu of every page that way, nearest first, each with its site's icon. Picking a row calls `go(to:)`, so it's one step however far back. A click still goes one page.

- `Tab.pages(back:)` and `Tab.go(to:)` hand out the back-forward list without exposing the `PageView`.
- `Door` takes an optional `held` closure. The hold is a `LongPressGesture` beside the button; an `opened` flag stops the press that opened the menu from also clicking. The right-click is a small AppKit view over the door that answers the hit test only for `.rightMouseDown`, so clicks and hover still reach the button.
- `Rewind.menu` builds the `NSMenu` when it opens rather than when the toolbar draws: the doors only redraw when `canGoBack` flips, so a menu built at draw time would often be a page behind. That's also why the right-click skips SwiftUI's `.contextMenu`.

Tried by hand in a local build: hold and right-click both open the list, picking a row goes there, and a plain click still goes one step.

items.title: Pages at 120 Hz: never, on power, or always
items.author: theosementa
items.decision: Adopt after baseline measurements

Settings › General › Pages at 120 Hz was a switch; it is now a Never / On power / Always control, like Appearance. On power draws pages at 120 Hz while the Mac is on its adapter (or has no battery) and drops back to 60 on battery, following the adapter as it is plugged in or pulled (IOKit's power-source notification, added to the run loop the first time On power is chosen).

- `FastPages` enum in FrameRate.swift; `FrameRate.mode` is what Settings says, `FrameRate.fast` (and WebKit's flag handling) works as before and is re-evaluated from it.

Tested: `swift build` with no warnings, `swift test` passes (47 tests). Not tried on a laptop unplugging, which needs a MacBook on battery.

Trade-off: any power source other than the battery (adapter, UPS) counts as on power.

items.title: Two fingers slide the page back and forward, as in Safari
items.author: theosementa
items.decision: Closed without merge flag: inspect before reuse
items.note: No adoption recommendation from closed state alone; may be declined, superseded, partially incorporated or incorporated outside GitHub merge.
items.body:
## What

Two fingers sideways now slide the page back or forward the way Safari does: WebKit's own gesture (`allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures`), with the previous page following the fingers. A new switch, **Settings › General › Swipe between pages**, turns it off; off, two fingers sideways do nothing at all. Mouse side buttons and the Logi swipe (`swipe(with:)`) still go back and forward either way, since they aren't two-finger trackpad gestures.

The setting is applied to pages already open as well as new ones (`PageView.applyGestures()`, run over `Web.pages` when the switch changes, and from `build()`).

## Why it is on by default

This departs from CONTRIBUTING's "off until someone turns it on" rule on purpose: it was asked for explicitly, and it is what every Mac browser does. Before, Search had its own disc gesture and WebKit's was forced off.

## Hold a swipe to pick from history

That option needs the custom disc: WebKit's slide has no hook to show a list of pages mid-gesture, and running both would go back twice. So the three states are:

| Swipe between pages | Hold a swipe to pick from history | Two fingers do |
|---|---|---|
| on | off | WebKit's slide (default) |
| on | on | the disc and the list, as before (WebKit's slide is off while it is on) |
| off | n/a | nothing (the history row is hidden) |

The history row says that the page doesn't slide while it is on. The disc code in `PageView.scrollWheel` now only runs when it is the one in charge, so the two can't both fire. `Swipe.calm` (rubber-banding) is untouched.

## Also touched

- `./bench pull` feeds synthetic wheel events that only the disc reads, so it now switches the held swipe on for the length of the pull (test runs only) and restores it after. Its help text says so.
- Comments in Swipe.swift and Tab.swift updated to match.
- CHANGELOG line under Unreleased.

## How tested

`swift build` (no new warnings from the touched files) and `swift test` (47 tests, 0 failures). The slide itself needs a real trackpad and I couldn't drive one from here, so that part is untested by hand: worth a quick swipe with the switch on, off, and with Hold a swipe on.

Every other icon lookup (Stage, Omnibox, bookmarks, notifications, extension shims, session restore, `arrived`, `relook`, `adopt`) already goes through `Favicons.site` since #413.

## Tested

items.title: Round site card corners on macOS 26
items.author: mihxlko
items.decision: Adapt small polish
items.note: Always mask site-card material on macOS 26. Browse autocomplete changed this surface/type, so do not blindly apply original hunk.
items.body: ## Summary On macOS 26.5, the site card's material and shadow extend past its rounded border as a square in light and dark mode. The existing rounded mask is applied only before macOS 26; this change applies it on macOS 26 too. The card's color, material, and layout are unchanged. ## Screenshots Before and after in light and dark mode: Also checked the card opening above the tab and the expanded “Connection is secure” view in both modes: ## Testing - `swift build` and `./build.sh` completed. items.title: Open links from pinned tabs in a peek, as Arc does
items.author: bent2685
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: #581 keeps pins on-site through optional peek. Depends on correctly preserving OAuth/popups and same-site navigation.
items.body:
## The problem

Pinned tabs are the pages you keep open all day: Google, Gmail, Notion, a dashboard. But a link clicked inside a pin takes the pin itself to that link. Search on Google, click a result, and the Google pin is now a news site. To get back you either press Back a few times or double-click the pin to go home. Either way, the pin stops being the page you pinned.

The shift-click peek (Settings › General) already fixes this one link at a time, but only if you remember to hold Shift on every click. In a pin, holding Shift is what you want almost every time, so it ends up being something you have to keep in your head.

The "Links from a pin open a new tab" item in the roadmap comes from the same problem. Opening a new tab does keep the pin in place, but each quick look adds a tab to the row, and those tabs have to be closed by hand later.

## Proposal

Arc's way: **a link from a pinned tab to another site opens in a peek**.

- A new setting, **off by default**, for example Settings › Tabs › *Open links from pins in a peek*.
- When it is on and a link in a pinned tab leads to a **different site** (a different registrable domain), the navigation is cancelled and the link opens in the existing peek panel (`Browser.peek(_:from:)`). Esc, a click beside the panel, or its × puts the page away, and the pin is still where it was. ⌘↩ keeps the page as a tab, as it does today.
- Links within the **same site** go as they always have, so moving around inside Gmail, Notion or Google stays in the pin.
- `target="_blank"` links from a pin get the same treatment in `createWebViewWith`. Real popups are left alone, meaning windows opened with size or toolbar features (OAuth / "Sign in with…"): they need `window.opener`.
- Only plain left-clicks count. ⌘-click, middle-click and the context menu keep doing what they do now. Shift-click keeps working as it does today.
- Inside a peek, links just go, as they do now.

The change is small: one check in `decidePolicyFor navigationAction` next to the shift-click branch, one in `createWebViewWith`, and the pref. If this sounds right, I'm happy to send a PR.

items.title: Proposal: optional native UI smoke tests for import and Find
items.author: quanru
items.decision: Historical issue: closed; not independently revalidated
items.note: Closed state alone does not establish resolution; inspect body/discussion if reopening.
items.body:
Search already has Swift coverage for browser decisions, but a passing test does not show that the native import dialog, bookmark list and Find bar work together on screen. I would like to propose an **optional, three-case native UI smoke suite** using Midscene Test on GitHub-hosted Intel Macs.

The proposed scope is deliberately small:
- Import a local exported bookmark file and open its folder.
- Import it twice, assert both visible import outcomes, and verify unique final entries.
- Find a word on a local page and assert the visible counter and highlights.

Operations use `aiAct`; every case has `aiAssert`. Each case gets a private app/probe directory and fixtures. Model configuration is opt-in: PRs run model-free checks, while configured trusted main/manual runs can use a model. The JavaScript packages are test tooling, with no dependency added to the shipped browser. Pages is optional; native HTML artifacts remain usable without it.

Working evidence at the same implementation commit: [full run 1](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/37879966874), [full run 2](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/37881379260), and [native report](https://quanru.github.io/Search/runs/37881379260/1/native/index.html). Both runs passed 61 Swift tests and all three visual cases. A separate [wrong-assertion demonstration](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/37883270280) failed at the intended aiAssert and retained its report, screenshot and exact-step link.

The tradeoff is a new optional model service and hosted Mac time, plus maintenance of the visual fixtures. This is smoke coverage, not a replacement for Swift tests or evidence of a long-term failure rate. I propose reviewing the small test-only WebKit synchronization fix separately, then deciding whether this optional layer earns its maintenance cost. The integration also has a DEBUG-only visible-probe seam; ordinary browser behavior stays unchanged.

items.title: Make WebKit download fixtures deterministic on hosted Macs
items.author: quanru
items.decision: Adopt into CI work
items.note: Test-only download delegate/fixture races and bounded runner. Independent of declined model-backed #580. Adapt hard-coded seven-test discovery as suite evolves.
items.body:
Hosted Mac runs can lose a WebKit download callback between `startDownload` returning and the test attaching its delegate. Cancellation tests can also receive their first progress only after the short fixture response has already finished. These are fixture races that obscure the download lifecycle assertions.

This test-only patch attaches the delegate inside the callback, holds the cancellation transfer open until fixture teardown, and adds a bounded CI deadline with useful state diagnostics. `Tests/run-ci-tests.py` runs the 54 other tests together and all 7 download journeys in fresh processes. Every download assertion still runs; there are no retries or skips.

Earlier dependent-branch validation: [hosted execution 1](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/37879966874) and [hosted execution 2](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/37881379260) passed all 61 Swift tests using this runner. These executions are on the dependent integration branch containing this exact patch; they are not standalone runs of this PR head.

This is independently useful test infrastructure and can be reviewed before the optional native UI proposal in #578. The diff is limited to two download fixtures and the runner; shipped browser sources are unchanged.

Dependent optional UI suite: #580. This fixture patch can be merged independently.

## Standalone current-head validation — 2026-10-10

[Exact PR-head hosted Intel Mac job](https://github.com/quanru/Search/actions/runs/38022476017/job/114126243517) passed **all 61 Swift tests at `f831297ee22a1585100c4583e6dd13e0918bbf4d`**, including all seven download cases in their own processes. The other 54 tests ran together. No retries, skipped download cases, model calls or app-source modifications were used. This closes the earlier evidence gap where only the dependent integration branch had been run.

items.title: Pins stay on their site: links to other sites open in a peek (#577)
items.author: bent2685
items.decision: Later
items.note: Optional cross-site peek from pins. Check registrable domains, OAuth popup exceptions, modifiers and same-site navigation.
items.body:
Closes #577.

## The problem

A pinned tab is meant to be a place you come back to: Gmail, GitHub, Google. Today, clicking a link in it to another site navigates the pin itself. After a few clicks the pin is somewhere else entirely, and getting back means pressing Back a few times or re-opening the site. `target=_blank` links and `window.open` from a pin open new tabs in the tab bar, which clutters the row. Pin as Row tabs behave the same way.

Arc solves this with Peek, and this PR brings that behaviour to Search, behind a switch.

## What it does

A new switch, **Settings › Tabs › Pins stay on their site**, is off by default (`pins.peek`). When it is on, the following applies to pinned tabs, both squares and Pin as Row:

| In a pin | Before | With the switch on |
|---|---|---|
| Plain click on a link to **another site** | the pin navigates away | opens in a **peek** over the page; the pin stays put |
| `target=_blank` / `window.open` to another site | new tab in the row | opens in the peek (the opener is kept, so `window.opener` still works) |
| Link that goes out **through the site itself** (Google results via `google.com/goto` → 302) | the pin navigates away | opens in the peek |
| Link within the **same site** (same registrable domain) | navigates | navigates, unchanged |
| ⌘W | the pin rests where it was | the pin goes back to the **URL it was pinned at** |

Modified clicks (⇧, ⌘, ⌥, ⌃) and real popups (windows with features) keep their existing behaviour. The peek itself is the existing Peek: Esc, a click outside or × closes it, and ⌘↩ keeps it as a tab.

### Visual polish
- **Badge on the pin.** While a peek is open, the pin it came from shows the peek's site icon in a small rounded rectangle: on the top-right corner of a pin square, and at the end of a pin row. Under the pointer, the row's close button takes its place.
- **Solid peek panel.** Until its page drew, the panel was only a border over the page behind. It now has a solid, theme-aware background from the first frame.
- **Skeleton loader.** A text-free page skeleton (top bar, heading, image, lines of text) with a shimmer, shown until the page's first frame is drawn. It only appears after 150 ms, so fast pages never flash it. For performance, the shapes are drawn once into a single layer (`drawingGroup`) and the shimmer is one gradient moving under a mask, so nothing is re-laid out per frame. It is static when Reduce Motion is on.

## How it works

- **`Browser.decide`**: a plain `.linkActivated` main-frame navigation from a pin to a different registrable domain (`Vault.registrable`) is cancelled and handed to `peek(_:from:)`. The "here" side comes from `backForwardList.currentItem` rather than `webView.url`: at a server redirect WebKit asks again, still as `.linkActivated`, with `webView.url` already pointing at the redirect target. That is why Google results were not caught at first.
- **`followsPeek`**: after a peek, Google's script also tries to send the pin to the same place (`.other`). Navigations of that kind to the site just peeked are turned away for 3 s.
- **`createWebViewWith`**: for a non-popup new window from a pin, `peekWindow` builds the peek's tab on the configuration WebKit hands over and returns its web view, so the page loads straight into the peek.
- **`Browser.close`**: a pin rests at `tab.home` when the switch is on (`Tab.rest(at:)`).
- **`Browser.peekFrom`** records which tab the peek came from, for the badge. **`Tab.painted`** is set from the existing first-frame hook (`PageView.onFirstFrame`) and drives the skeleton.
- The bench `probe` reports `peekFrom`, for tests.

## Tests

The new **`Tests/pin_peek.py`** runs 23 checks against local servers on two sites (`127.0.0.1` and `localhost`, plus a same-site 302 hop):
- cross-site link → peek, the pin stays, and the badge is attributed to the pin
- `_blank`, `_blank` through a redirect, and `window.open` → peek
- same-site link → navigates in the pin
- server redirect → peek, with no failure page
- the script fallback is turned away
- ⌘W → back to the pinned URL, and the page wakes there
- Pin as Row: the same, including `_blank`, plus the badge
- closing the peek clears the badge
- unpinned tabs are unaffected
- switch off → the old behaviour, both for links and for ⌘W

Also tried by hand on Google (whose results go out through `google.com/goto`), with pin squares and pin rows.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

items.title: Arc's pinned list comes in with the shape Arc gave it
items.author: Chahine-tech
items.decision: Maintainer landing reference verified in Browse ancestry
items.note: Inspect current code; the landing may be an adapted subset, not the original PR unchanged.
items.body:
Closes #478, the half left after #494, and takes the second reading you picked there.

Arc's pinned list is split the way Arc itself holds it. `Browser.opened` already hands each page over with the folder it came from, or nil for one Arc keeps loose, so the split reads straight off it:

- a page Arc keeps loose is a page you keep, which is what a row is for, and comes in as one;
- a page it filed in a folder stays a tab in a group of that name, since a pin is never in a group and the folder's name is the thing that would be lost.

With Pinned rows off, nothing is split: the whole list comes in as tabs, as it does after #494.

The sheet says which before anything is brought over, as you suggested: with rows on the line reads "…the favourites as pins, its pinned pages as rows under them, and the ones it filed in a folder as tabs in a group of that name", and without them it reads as it did.

A loose page whose site is already pinned is left alone, by the same rule #500 gave the favourites.

## Checked

`Tests/arc_rows.py`, in its own world with the `sv.use` you added when you merged #494. A made-up Arc with a favourite, a page kept loose, and two filed in a folder named SRE:

```
  ok   the favourite is a square
  ok   the page Arc kept loose is a row
  ok   the two it filed are tabs in a group of that name
  ok   and the row is not a tab of its own
  ok   with rows off, no pin is kept as one
  ok   and the page Arc kept loose is a tab again
6 passed, 0 failed
```

On main, from a worktree, the two about rows fail and the rest passes, including both of the rows-off cases, so nothing that already worked is being guarded by accident:

```
  FAIL the page Arc kept loose is a row []
  FAIL and the row is not a tab of its own  [example.com/, iana.org/, rfc-editor.org/, ietf.org/]
4 passed, 2 failed
```

`swift build` adds no warnings.

One thing worth saying: the line in the sheet keeps your "— each a space here" as it was. I moved the sentence into a small function so it could vary with the setting, and left your wording alone.

items.title: A browser macOS won't let Search read is reported as having nothing in it
items.author: Chahine-tech
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: Prefer #507 then updated #415, which now distinguishes denied/missing/empty sources and adds a session folder picker. #603 provides a narrower message using broad Full Disk Access guidance.
items.body:
Bring Things Over lists Arc and Opera, not Chrome, and says underneath:

> Chrome is on this Mac, but nothing of it was found in ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome.

Chrome is installed, open, and its bookmarks bar is full. Nothing of it is missing. The read is refused, not empty.

## What is happening

macOS keeps one app's data from another until it is allowed, and Chrome's folder is one it keeps. Running the same call `Source.profiles` makes, on this Mac today:

```
Google/Chrome : app installed true, profiles found 0,
                NSCocoaErrorDomain 257 / NSPOSIXErrorDomain 1 (Operation not permitted)
Arc/User Data : app installed true, profiles found 1, no error
```

`Import.swift` reads the folder with `(try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(…)) ?? []`, so a refusal and an empty folder become the same value. `Chromium.unreadable()` then keeps every browser whose app is installed and whose `profiles` came back empty, and says nothing was found there.

So the one thing a person needs to know, that macOS hasn't let Search look, is the one thing the sentence doesn't say.

## What it costs

A person arriving from Chrome, which is most people, reads that Search found nothing of it and stops. I spent an evening rearranging what Arc had, and rewriting my bookmarks folders, before finding out that Chrome had simply never been read. The bar I was trying to rebuild was in Chrome all along.

## The view already has the shape for this

Three lines above, the Safari note explains a macOS restriction and what to do instead:

> Safari — macOS keeps its data from other apps: in Safari, File › Export Browsing Data, then bring the file in below.

A browser macOS is holding back deserves the same: that it is not allowed, rather than that there is nothing there, and where to allow it.

Seen today on this Mac, macOS 27, with the sheet's own words in the screenshot below. Happy to send it as a pull request.

items.title: The folded column comes and goes as quickly as Arc's and Dia's sidebars
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Measure then adapt
items.note: Faster fold springs/grace. Published timing is not a Browse measurement; test right sidebar, top strip and Reduce Motion.
items.body:
The folded column felt slow to go away, and slow to turn around when the pointer came back halfway. I timed it against Arc and Dia to see by how much.

## Measured

Same Mac, blank page, 120fps screen capture while a script drives the pointer to the window's left edge and away. Medians of 5 runs, from the moment the pointer arrives or leaves to 90% of the slide.

| | Arc 1.168 | Dia 1.52 | Search before | Search now |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Out | 228ms | 286ms | 325ms+ | 171ms |
| Back in | 78ms | 174ms | 400ms+ | 159ms |
| Pointer returns mid-hide, stops retreating | n/a | n/a | 155ms | 10ms |

"Before" was measured on an intermediate build that was already quicker than `main` (springs 0.26/0.2, grace 0.2s), so `main` is slower still. Arc and Dia finish hiding in under 80ms once they start, so the pointer can't catch them halfway.

## Change

- **`Motion.fold(out:)` / `Motion.folding(out:)`** (`Design.swift`): the fold's own springs, out 0.14 / 0.86 and in 0.13 / 1 (critically damped, since nothing is arriving to settle). Glide (0.34 / 0.82) stays for everything else.
- **Peek, ⌘S and Settings › hides** (`Fold.swift`) animate on them.
- **The window's buttons** in `Fold.slide` read the same numbers instead of a hand-copied 0.34 / 0.82, so they can't drift from the column.
- **`Fold.grace`** from 0.3s to 0.065s. With the ~15ms before the slide starts, the column begins to go about when Dia's does. Arc doesn't wait at all; the grace still covers a hand overshooting on the way back in.
- CHANGELOG line under Fixed.

## Side effect

⌘S folding and unfolding the whole layout now uses the quicker springs too. If that reads as abrupt, `toggleFold` can go back to `Motion.glide` on its own.

## Tested

- `swift build` and `./build.sh` pass.
- Timed in the built app at every step, as above.
- Not tested: the strip across the top, and the column on the right. Both go through the same `peek` and `slide` code.

## Noticed, not changed

The column takes ~90ms to start moving on every peek, with no dwell set (`sidebar.hides = 0`). I think that's `SideBar` being built from scratch each time it's inserted, but I haven't confirmed it. It's still quicker than Arc's (~130ms) and Dia's (~195ms) deliberate waits, so I left it.

items.title: The folded column and tab bar are kept while away and slid out, not built anew on every peek
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Measure then adapt
items.note: Keep folded chrome mounted to avoid layout churn; assess retained memory/accessibility and add scroll-on-peek behavior from #599 interaction.
items.body:
The folded column waited about 90ms after the pointer reached the edge before it moved, with no dwell set. It was being built again, every row, on every peek. This keeps it mounted while folded and slides it in, and does the same for the tab bar across the top.

Independent of #585 (the fold's springs and grace): based on `main`, touches a different part of `Fold.swift`, and either can merge first.

## Cause

`Fold` inserted `SideBar` with `if folding, prefs.sidebar, browser.peeking` and a `.move` transition, so each peek created the whole column and each hide threw it away. Timed with a run-loop observer, the main thread spent **55 to 73ms** between `peek(true)` and the end of the commit; hiding took about 10ms. A profile puts that time in SwiftUI's layout of the new subtree (sizing every row, the `ForEach` making its items, a layer per row), not in Search's own code.

The tell: when the pointer came back while the column was still leaving, the old one was still in the tree, and that commit took 13 to 20ms.

## Change

- While folded, `SideBar` stays mounted and sits off the window's edge by `prefs.sideWidth`. A peek animates `.offset` and the shadow's `strength` (the same `FoldShadow`, now a plain modifier) in place of the insertion transition.
- `.allowsHitTesting(browser.peeking)`, so the column takes no clicks while it's away or sliding.
- The strip across the top gets the same treatment: `TabBar` stays mounted above the window's top edge, offset by `Metrics.strip` (its exact height).
- The `casting` transition has no callers left, so it's removed.
- CHANGELOG line under Fixed.

## Measured

Same Mac, blank page, 120fps screen capture with a script driving the pointer, medians of 5 runs, both builds with #585's springs:

| | Rebuilt per peek | Kept mounted |
|---|---|---|
| Main thread, peek to commit | ~60ms | ~14ms |
| Pointer at edge → column moving | 96ms | ~51ms |
| Out, to 90% | 180ms | ~135ms |
| Back in, to 90% | 172ms | ~172ms |

Strip across the top, same method, both on `main`'s springs (so slower overall than with #585):

| | Rebuilt per peek | Kept mounted |
|---|---|---|
| Main thread, peek to commit | not timed | ~22ms |
| Pointer at edge → strip moving | 237ms | 211ms |
| Back in, to 90% | 548ms | 550ms |

The strip saves less because a row of tabs is cheaper to build than the column. Most of what's left is the 150ms dwell it keeps on purpose, since the menu bar is just above it.

## Tradeoff: accessibility

While folded, the column (or the strip) stays in the accessibility tree, off-screen. Before, a folded one wasn't there at all. I tried `.accessibilityHidden(!browser.peeking)`, and then the same toggle delayed until the slide had finished: either way, some commits took 60 to 120ms where they had taken 10ms, I think because accessibility clients re-walk the tree on every change. The comment in `Fold` says so. If hiding it matters more than the latency, that toggle is the place to put it back.

## Not changed

- A peek doesn't scroll the list to the active tab, on `main` as well as here. The ScrollView's `onAppear` `scrollTo` doesn't seem to take on the folded column. Not looked into.
- A mounted column runs `onAppear` once per fold, not once per peek. The only hooks there are `SpaceSwipe.start`, which installs its monitor once and picks the window per gesture, and that `scrollTo`.

## Tested

- `swift build` and `./build.sh` pass; applies cleanly to `main`.
- In the built app: timed as above, and screenshots of the column and of the strip, out and folded (no shadow left along the edge).
- Not tested: the column on the right, full screen, VoiceOver.

items.title: A pin moved to another space stays there, after a relaunch too
items.author: karadoganyi
items.decision: Adopt early
items.note: Persists moved pin in destination pins.json and correct pin tier. Independent of global-pins #463; strong relaunch regression.
items.body:
Split out of #463, as asked, for 1.0.5.

## The bug

Move to Space on a pin put the tab in the destination space's row, but never added it to that space's list in pins.json. The next rebuild of that space's pins found it in no list and closed it. So a pin moved to a space you don't open before quitting was gone after a relaunch.

## The fix

`finishMove` adds the moved pin to the destination space's list in pins.json too, with squares ahead of rows (as `Browser.tiered` keeps them). The tab itself goes into the row at the same place: a square after the squares, a row after the rows. Before, a square moved into a space with row pins went after the rows. The source space's list loses the pin through `writeSession`, as before.

## Checked

- `Tests/pin_to_space.py` is new, with 6 checks in a hidden test world. Two spaces; the second already has a row pin and is never opened. A square pin is moved there, then the app quits and relaunches. The test checks pins.json (the pin listed under the destination, ahead of its row, and gone from the source) and both spaces' pins after the relaunch.
  - On current main, the pins.json check and the relaunch check fail. With only the first half of the fix (the pin listed, but appended after the row), the order check fails. With this change, 6/6 pass.
- Also run: `Tests/pin_tiers.py` 32/32, `Tests/fresh_window.py` 7/7, `Tests/arc_pins.py` 7/7, `Tests/split_view.py` 92/92. `./build.sh` builds with no new warnings.

items.title: Keep checking for extension updates while Search stays open
items.author: BryanZaneee
items.decision: Adopt early
items.note: Single hourly timer reuses 20-hour update throttle; per-extension in-flight guard. User-owned branch available; not already in main.
items.body:
Search only checked for extension updates at startup, so a browser left open for days never checked again. The extension manager now schedules one hourly timer and reuses the existing 20-hour throttle, download verification, permission approval, and replacement flow.

A per-extension in-flight guard prevents another check from starting the same update while a request or permission prompt is pending. Failure releases the guard so a later check can retry. There are no new settings or dependencies.

Validation on macOS 27.0.1 / Apple Swift 6.4:
- Both scheduling and overlap regressions passed using the real timer callback, controlled timestamps, and intercepted requests. Each regression also fails when its corresponding production fix is removed. No live extension was downloaded or updated.
- Five extension-file replacement checks passed, including preservation of the installed copy when replacement fails.
- Debug and release app builds passed. The compiler warning set matches across the independent branches; the changed code adds none.
- Full Swift suite: 62 passed, one failed. The same `ExtensionFileAccessTests.testFilesAreNeverGrantedButSitesAre` failure reproduces on unmodified main `59c1b4e`: this WebKit does not grant the fixture's file pattern.

A day elapsed during sleep is simulated by advancing the stored check time and firing the timer; real sleep/wake and a multi-day soak were not run. Live store downloads and permission-dialog interaction were not rerun; their existing implementation is unchanged.

Fixes #539.

items.title: A website whose name starts with 10. or 192.168. is opened over http, not https
items.author: Dev-next-gen
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: #592 is the focused fix, overlapping one commit of #603. Direct parser reproduction also exposed 172.16.foo.com using HTTP.
items.body:
`Address.url(from:)` picks the scheme for anything typed into the address field, and `Browser.destination(for:)` hands back its URL as the page to open. It chooses plain http for two cases written as string prefixes:

```swift
|| host.hasPrefix("192.168.")
|| host.hasPrefix("10.")
```

Those are tests on a name, not on an address, so they also catch websites. `10.io`, `10.ai`, `10.org`, `10.net`, `10.fr` and `10.co.uk` are all registered and resolve today, and `10.0.0.1.example.com` is a website like any other.

**What I did.** I compiled `Sources/Search/Address.swift` on its own with `swiftc`, the way `Tests/HistoryRegression/run.sh` compiles `History.swift`, and called `Address.url(from:)`:

```
10.io                     ->  http://10.io
10.org/about              ->  http://10.org/about
10.0.0.1.example.com      ->  http://10.0.0.1.example.com
192.168.1.1.example.com   ->  http://192.168.1.1.example.com
```

**What I expected.** `https://10.io`, as for every other website typed the same way. `example.com` gets https, and so does `172.15.0.1`.

**What happened instead.** Plain http. `http://10.io/` answers 200 with no redirect to https, so the page arrives unencrypted and stays that way. Nothing downstream puts the scheme back: `destination(for:)` returns that URL as it is.

The right shape is already in the repo twice. `privateRange`, in this same file, requires four numbers before it calls 172.16/12 private, and `Dialogs.isLoopback` does the same, for the reason written above it:

> Only the names that can't mean anything else: localhost, and the loopback addresses written as addresses, four numbers and nothing more, so 127.0.0.1.example.com is a website like any other.

A server on this Mac or on the local network should still get http, and does with that shape: `10.0.0.1`, `10.255.255.254:9000`, `192.168.1.1`, `172.16.0.1`, `localhost:3000` and `printer.local` all keep it.

No macOS version to give: this is Foundation only, and the scheme is decided before anything touches the network or AppKit. Happy to send the fix as a pull request.

items.title: Use native video PiP to keep webpages usable and prevent video cutoff
items.author: BryanZaneee
items.decision: Implemented in Browse
items.note: Native video PiP branch already in main. Upstream #593 remains open; Browse PR #2 is also open despite ancestry containing its branch.
items.body:
## Problem

On macOS 27.0.1, I encountered these problems while testing video PiP:
_I attached screenshots of what I am talking about below as well!_

- Opening PiP makes the rest of the webpage unavailable (e.g. YouTube comments while PiP is used).
- Resizing can crop the video or distort its aspect ratio.
- Switching tabs away and back to the tab hosting the PiP ends manually opened PiP.
- Paused videos cannot enter PiP.
- Returning the video can leave a blank page until resizing or switching tabs.

To reproduce, open a video, enter PiP with ⇧⌘P, resize it, switch tabs and return, then return the video inline. Also try entering PiP while paused and you'll see these issues reflected.

Related: #543, #257 and #547. #547 improves geometry within the existing custom floating-window approach; I am proposing replacing that approach with native WebKit PiP, as this will fix all the above issues as well as follows the project’s preference for a small, dependency-free WebKit implementation in place of the current custom code.

## Implementation ready for review!

I have a native WebKit PiP implementation ready for review that addresses these cases. It replaces the custom floating panel, page-restyling code, and playback controls with macOS's native presentation, reducing custom code without adding dependencies. The current patch removes 1,504 lines and adds 687 across code, tests, and documentation, thus a massive reduction.

It also adds an optional **PiP button**, off by default in Settings. When enabled, it appears beside Bookmarks when the page has a PiP-capable video and provides a return action while PiP is active.

Verification includes 55 passing PiP regression checks and 92 passing Split View checks. The implementation uses a guarded private WebKit preference; older macOS runtime behavior remains unverified.

Would this direction fit the project? I can submit the implementation for review. I tried to emphasize clean, lightwieght code and the native nature of the program with the native PiP implementation.

<details>
<summary>Screenshots: before / after</summary>

The first before screenshot shows both problems: the webpage is unavailable, and the video is cut off inside the floating window.

| Before: webpage unavailable and video cropped | After: webpage usable with native PiP |
| --- | --- |
| ![Old PiP hides the webpage and cuts off the video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BryanZaneee/Search/d1649e678541a63fb97aa7fab8b060883aa8425a/before-page-unavailable.png) | ![Native PiP leaves the webpage usable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BryanZaneee/Search/d1649e678541a63fb97aa7fab8b060883aa8425a/after-native-pip.png) |

| Before: blank page on return | After: video back inline |
| --- | --- |
| ![Blank webpage after returning the video](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BryanZaneee/Search/d1649e678541a63fb97aa7fab8b060883aa8425a/before-blank-return.png) | ![Video and webpage visible after return](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BryanZaneee/Search/d1649e678541a63fb97aa7fab8b060883aa8425a/after-return.png) |

</details>

items.title: A website whose name starts with 10. or 192.168. is opened over https
items.author: Dev-next-gen
items.decision: Adopt early
items.note: Require literal IPv4 for private ranges; focused tests and no feature changes. Prefer to the same fix bundled in #603.
items.body:
Typing a website whose name begins with `10.` or `192.168.` opens it over plain http.

`Address.url(from:)` decides the scheme, and `Browser.destination(for:)` returns its URL as the page to open. Two of its tests for a local server were string prefixes rather than address checks:

```swift
|| host.hasPrefix("192.168.")
|| host.hasPrefix("10.")
```

A name is not an address, so those also caught websites. `10.io`, `10.ai`, `10.org`, `10.net`, `10.fr` and `10.co.uk` are all registered and resolve today, and `10.0.0.1.example.com` is a website like any other. `http://10.io/` answers 200 without redirecting to https, and nothing between `destination(for:)` and the page puts the scheme back, so what arrives is unencrypted and stays that way. Every other website typed the same way gets https.

`privateRange` now covers all three private ranges and requires four numbers and nothing more, which is the shape it already had for 172.16/12 and the one `Dialogs.isLoopback` uses for the same reason: "so 127.0.0.1.example.com is a website like any other". A server on this Mac or on the local network is unaffected.

I compiled `Sources/Search/Address.swift` on its own with `swiftc`, the way `Tests/HistoryRegression/run.sh` compiles `History.swift`, and called `Address.url(from:)`. Before, four cases were wrong and nothing else was:

```
FAIL: 10.io became http://10.io, expected https://10.io
FAIL: 10.org/about became http://10.org/about, expected https://10.org/about
FAIL: 10.0.0.1.example.com became http://10.0.0.1.example.com, expected https://10.0.0.1.example.com
FAIL: 192.168.1.1.example.com became http://192.168.1.1.example.com, expected https://192.168.1.1.example.com
```

After, all of them pass, and so do `10.0.0.1`, `10.255.255.254:9000`, `192.168.1.1`, `172.16.0.1`, `172.31.255.254`, `127.0.0.1:8080`, `0.0.0.0:8080`, `localhost:3000` and `printer.local` keeping http, `example.com`, `172.15.0.1` and `172.32.0.1` getting https, and `hello world` and `todo` still being searches. `Tests/HistoryRegression/run.sh`, which compiles `Address.swift` too and exercises it through address completion, passes unchanged. Those checks are in `Tests/AddressRegression/run.sh`, in the same shape as the History runner, so they run without building the app.

Fixes #590

Found by a defect-hunting pipeline I build and run ([Dev-next-gen](https://github.com/Dev-next-gen)), using Claude Code with Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.

items.author: BryanZaneee

items.body:
Could Search add **Copy Clean Link** beside Copy Address in a tab’s right-click menu? It would make sharing a page without common tracking parameters a little easier:

**Before:**
`https://example.com/article?id=42&utm_source=newsletter#details`

**After:**
→ `https://example.com/article?id=42#details`

I’d like to keep this tiny and native: reuse the existing menu and clipboard code, use Foundation for local URL processing, and add no dependencies or network requests. Since it only runs when selected from the right-click menu, I propose no Settings toggle, subject to your agreement with that exception to the default-off guideline.

Start with an explicit list: `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_term`, `utm_content`, `gclid`, and `fbclid`. Preserve functional and unknown parameters, their ordering and encoding, and fragments. Copy recognized signed URLs and uncertain input unchanged. No rule list can detect every signed URL; ordinary Copy Address would remain unchanged.

Tests would use synthetic URLs and isolated test worlds, checking actual copied bytes without touching the user’s clipboard.

Would this scope and initial cleanup list fit the project? I’d wait for agreement on the rules before implementing it.

items.title: Feature request: domain-to-Space link routing with internal overrides
items.author: AdityaAmitK
items.decision: Covered by active work
items.note: #596 implements routing before the first request. Useful for eventual browser/email account separation, after Spaces privacy and session behavior are stable.
items.body:
External links currently open in whichever Space is selected. When switching between personal and work browsing, this can send a link to the wrong account/session.

Could Search support an optional domain-to-Space rule list in Settings → Routing?

For example:
- `youtube.com` → Personal
- `github.com` → Work
- `docs.example.com` → Research

The feature would start disabled with an empty rule list. Users could add, edit, disable, or remove rules and select an existing Space. Domains would include their subdomains, with the most specific enabled rule winning. Support exact local hosts (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`) and an optional port, so local development servers can use a chosen Space. Leaving the port blank covers all ports; a port-specific rule overrides that fallback.

External routing should apply to URLs opened from other applications, including links that launch Search. The destination Space should be selected before the page's web view is created, so its first request uses that Space's session. Internal links should stay in the current Space by default. Add global choices to stay current, ask where to open, or route to the configured destination, plus per-domain overrides for each choice. For example, YouTube could always route to Personal while GitHub stays in whichever Space is currently selected. Routing should preserve the source tab and apply before the destination request uses an account session. User clicks, new-tab actions, address-bar navigation, bookmarks, and history are eligible; scripts, redirects, subframes, form submissions, downloads, and private tabs keep their existing behavior. If an enabled rule points to a deleted Space, the link should be blocked with a clear message rather than opened with another Space's session.

I have a working local prototype and a small implementation ready against current main, with no new dependencies. The upstream implementation leaves Search's updater unchanged.

### Prototype screenshots

Both screenshots use a disposable profile, sample rules, and generic Space names; there are no signed-in pages.

![Routing settings with sample rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdityaAmitK/search-space-routing/1f00b3dfa81d812d5d818c45d88b46be2126c494/assets/screenshots/routing-settings.png)

![Editing a rule and its destination](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdityaAmitK/search-space-routing/1f00b3dfa81d812d5d818c45d88b46be2126c494/assets/screenshots/routing-editor.png)

Implementation: [pull request #596](https://github.com/driceroland/Search/pull/596).


![Choosing a Space](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdityaAmitK/search-space-routing/1f00b3dfa81d812d5d818c45d88b46be2126c494/assets/screenshots/routing-ask.png)

items.title: Add domain-to-Space routing with configurable internal navigation
items.author: AdityaAmitK
items.decision: Later, valuable ecosystem feature
items.note: Route before first request to keep correct account cookies; larger internal navigation policy. Rebase after tab/window fixes, preserve POST/redirect/private exclusions.
items.body:
Links opened from other apps currently use the selected Space, which can load the wrong account/session. This adds optional domain rules in Settings → Routing and selects the destination before the first request, including URLs queued during launch.

Closes #595.

Internal user navigation stays in its current Space by default. Users can instead ask where to open or route automatically, globally or per domain. For example, YouTube can always route to Personal while GitHub stays in the current Space. Cross-Space routing opens a new destination tab and preserves the source; background link actions keep the source Space in front.

- Starts disabled with no rules. Add/edit, enable/disable, remove, global policy, per-domain overrides and native Space picker.
- Host/subdomain matching, most-specific rule, validated hosts and stable Space IDs. Supports localhost and loopback IPs with an optional port; exact-port rules override all-port rules for the same host.
- Legacy saved rules retain their enabled state and destinations; new internal settings default to current/inherit.
- User clicks, new-tab actions, address bar, bookmarks and history use routing. Scripts, redirects, subframes, forms, downloads and private tabs retain existing behavior.
- Missing destinations and disabled Spaces block automatic matched routes with a message. Search's updater is unchanged. No new dependencies.

### Validation

- Debug app build and 6 RoutingTests pass.
- 66 isolated internal browser checks pass, including first-request cookies, preserved source, single destination, overrides, legacy config, Ask cancellation, and script/POST/subframe/redirect/private exclusions.
- 5 external browser regression checks and 4 localhost external first-request-cookie checks pass.
- Tagged v1.0.4 port builds and passes policy, external browser and standalone profile-isolation checks.
- Native prototype: settings/editor, affirmative Ask, Current Space answer without another prompt, invalid-port rejection, blank-port acceptance and localhost internal destination.
- Earlier full suite: 63/64 passed. `ExtensionFileAccessTests.testFilesAreNeverGrantedButSitesAre` also fails on pristine main with the same WebKit assertion; unchanged by this feature. Native context-menu and bookmark/history paths were source-reviewed but are not in the runtime test matrix.

### Screenshots

Disposable generic Personal, Work and Research profile; prototype of the same UI. Upstream starts disabled and empty.

![Routing settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AdityaAmitK/search-space-routing/1f00b3dfa81d812d5d818c45d88b46be2126c494/assets/screenshots/routing-settings.png)

items.title: A folded column comes out on the tab you are on
items.author: oddharsh
items.decision: Adopt with #586 coordination
items.note: Delayed scroll-to-active row; author explicitly has not verified live result. Mounted sidebar needs scroll on peeking too, not just onAppear.
items.body:
With more tabs than the window holds, a peek at the folded column could come out with the tab you're on scrolled out of sight. The column means to centre it: the ScrollView's `onAppear` calls `proxy.scrollTo(active, anchor: .center)`. This makes that call one turn of the run loop later, as `TabBar.reveal` already does for the row across the top.

## What I saw

- **A real peek, live window:** about 40 tabs with the active one near the end. The column came out at the top of the list, the active row out of sight. Same on `main` and on #585.
- **The same column, made off screen** (`./bench column`, laid out before it's drawn): tab 38 of 40 active, and the list was scrolled down to it. So `scrollTo` from `onAppear` does work once the rows have their height.

## Why I think this is it

On a peek, the column is inserted partway through `withAnimation`, and `onAppear` can run before the new ScrollView has measured its rows. A `scrollTo` asked for then has nothing to scroll and is dropped. `TabBar.reveal` makes the same call through `DispatchQueue.main.async`, and the row across the top doesn't show this. I haven't confirmed the timing directly.

## Change

- `Side.swift`: the `onAppear` scroll waits one turn of the main queue. The scroll on a change of active tab (`onChange(of: browser.activeID)`) is unchanged.
- CHANGELOG line under Fixed.

## Tested

- `swift build` passes.
- **Not verified in the app.** A hidden test world never draws the column, so `film peek` can't show it, and I stopped short of driving a visible window with scripted keys. To check: fold with ⌘S, pick a tab low in a list longer than the window, move the pointer to the edge. The column should come out centred on that tab.

## With #586

#586 keeps the folded column mounted instead of building it on every peek, so this `onAppear` would run once per fold rather than once per peek. If both go in, a peek needs its own scroll when `peeking` turns true, made the same way, a turn later. I'd add that to #586 when it's rebased on the column rework.

items.title: AdBlock's background starts: webRequest listeners leave out the types WebKit doesn't know
items.author: FabianoC13
items.decision: Adapt with regression
items.note: Filter unsupported webRequest types for AdBlock. No test accompanies patch; add mixed/unsupported-only/unchanged listener cases and real extension startup check.
items.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"FabianoC13"} -->
_Requested by **fab**_

Before: the AdBlock extension loaded, but its background service worker stopped at startup, so element hiding and everything else the worker does never ran. Only the static network rules applied.

After: AdBlock's background starts and runs normally.

Chrome's webRequest resource types include `webtransport` and `webbundle`, which WebKit doesn't know, and WebKit rejects a whole listener that names either one. AdBlock listens for every type in the list.

How: the extension shims drop those two types from webRequest listener filters before handing them to WebKit.

items.title: Search gives back the memory an extension's rules took to build
items.author: FabianoC13
items.decision: Benchmark before adopting
items.note: Malloc pressure relief addresses retained allocator pages after rule compilation, not live leaks or site memory. Measure latency, CPU, battery and idle footprint; no test in patch.
items.body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"FabianoC13"} -->
_Requested by **fab**_

Before: with AdBlock installed, Search's memory footprint climbed past a gigabyte at launch and on every filter update, and stayed there (1,153 MB of footprint around 44 MB actually in use).

After: that memory goes back to the Mac within half a minute, and a launch with AdBlock settles at about 150 MB instead of 400 to 1,000.

WebKit compiles an extension's declarativeNetRequest rules inside the app's own process, all of them on every change, and malloc keeps the freed pages dirty afterwards.

How: a new `Trim.swift` reads the footprint every half minute and, past 64 MB of growth, asks malloc to return its empty pages; it also does so when the app goes to the background.

items.title: A paused video gives the media keys back
items.author: karadoganyi
items.decision: Gated polish
items.note: Paused-media muting interposes on page behavior. Test with native Browse PiP, real media keys and Spotify/Music; author has not verified actual external-app key handoff.
items.body:
Fixes #512, for the paused case, as discussed there.

Once a tab had played sound, the play/pause keys and AirPods taps went to it even after the video was paused, so Spotify or Music couldn't have them back until they played something again.

## Why

WebKit makes the app the Mac's Now Playing app as soon as unmuted media plays, and keeps that registration after a pause, with no setting to change it. A muted element is never the Now Playing one, though. With none left, WebKit gives up the registration and the Mac hands the keys back. That's what @jesusrp98 found, and WebKit's own readout confirms it:

| | Registered as Now Playing |
|---|---|
| playing | yes |
| paused | yes (the bug) |
| muted while paused | no |
| unmuted and playing again | yes |

## The fix

`MediaKeys.swift` adds a script in the page's own world, before any page script, in every frame, the same way `LiveRate` works.

- **When it acts:** a video or sound paused for **10 seconds** is muted underneath. A paused one can't be heard anyway.
- **What the page sees:** nothing. `muted` reads back what the page set. The `volumechange` from our mute is stopped by a window capture listener before the page hears it. If the page sets `muted` while the keys are handed back, it hears the change a moment later, and only when something changed, as WebKit would tell it.
- **Playing again:** it's unmuted before playback starts, whether from `play()` or a `play` event (native controls, the floating video). So it starts with its sound, and the keys come back to Search.
- **The page's own mute:** a page that muted it itself keeps it muted. If the video's own controls unmute it while the keys are handed back, that choice wins.
- **Media outside the page:** media the window never sees (`new Audio()`, or a player inside a shadow root) is watched on the element itself from its first `play()`.
- **Why 10 seconds:** pausing with the play/pause key and pressing it again a moment later still resumes the video instead of starting Spotify.
- **While media is playing:** the keys stay with Search; that part is WebKit's call. There's no Settings switch.

## Checked

- `Tests/media_keys.py` is new, with 28 checks in a hidden test world. It reads whether Search is registered as Now Playing from WebKit, through a test-only bench verb, `nowplaying` (WebKit's `_requestActiveNowPlayingSessionInfo:`, as WebKit's own tests use it).
  - **It covers:** a short pause keeps the keys; a long one gives them back with the page reading it unmuted and hearing no volume change; playing again with sound; the page's own mute; the page setting `muted` while the keys are handed back (same value: nothing heard, no loop from a listener that sets it again); the video's own controls unmuting it; an element taken out of the page while paused; `new Audio()`.
  - On current main, the two "the keys go back" checks fail. With this change, 28/28 pass in every run.
- On YouTube, in a hidden probe: playing, Search holds Now Playing with the video's title. After 13 seconds paused it's released, and both `video.muted` and the player's `isMuted()` still read false. Played again, it resumes with its sound and takes the keys back.
- A paused tab behind another tab gives the keys back too. I tried this with WebKit's real scheduling policy (`SEARCH_MEASURE`), since test runs otherwise set `inactiveSchedulingPolicy = .none`. It was released within 14 seconds.
- Also run: `Tests/float_video.py` 10/10, `Tests/live_rate.py`, `Tests/recording_pill.py` 9/9, `Tests/link_menu.py` 5/5, `Tests/split_view.py` 92/92. `swift test` gives the same result as main. `./build.sh` builds with no new warnings.

## Not checked

- I read WebKit's registration, not Spotify actually getting the keys back; @jesusrp98 saw macOS hand them back once the media was muted. @jesusrp98, if you can try a build: play Spotify and pause it, play then pause a YouTube video in Search, wait ten seconds, and press play/pause. Spotify should start.
- A page that added its own volume listener to a `new Audio()` element (or one in a shadow root) before playing it can hear one volume change when the keys are handed back; reading the values, nothing has changed.
